process: Findings were grouped into 14 clusters of related findings.

One agent per cluster reproduced each finding on this branch (commands in a copy of the repository, current file:line, or the external source fetched on 2026-11-03), tried to refute it, and assessed the reviewer's fix.
A second, independent agent per cluster re-checked the decisive evidence and tried to overturn each verdict in either direction.
Where the two disagreed on the verdict, a third agent re-checked the evidence and decided. Its verdict is final; both earlier positions are kept under audit and arbitration.
No agent changed the repository; experiments ran in copies.

owner_decisions.question: At the What next? menu, should a bare ok, yes or 👍 pick the ★ option and run it, the way Enter does in the Claude Code dialog? Or should only an explicit pick (the number, the option name, "run it", a dialog choice) start anything? Today one universal run read ok as Run it now. Also: should Fill placeholders collect the values and then run, as Run it now does today, or collect them, show the filled prompt and show the menu again?
owner_decisions.recommended: Explicit picks only; ok, 👍 or thanks gets "the prompt is ready" and nothing runs. Fill placeholders collects the values, shows the filled prompt and shows the menu again.

owner_decisions.question: What should "critique this prompt" or "what's missing from this prompt?" get? (A) Feedback only: the original's scores and its 3-5 biggest gaps, then an offer to build. (B) The normal flow, with "critique" dropped from the description; this needs a billed re-run of the 24 trigger tests. (C) The normal flow as today (a one-line gap summary, then questions), written down in SKILL.md and output-format.md:104.
owner_decisions.recommended: C if critique is not meant to be its own feature (cheapest, matches today's behavior); A if it is.

owner_decisions.question: In non-English replies, should the section headings, score rows, caveat line, What next? labels and reply keywords (ok, change N, deep) be translated, or stay in English as fixed labels?
owner_decisions.recommended: Translate them, as output-format.md:3 and questions.md:73 already say; make the universal core say the same.

owner_decisions.question: In the text format, should the ★ sit wherever it falls in a natural order (as the examples and README show), or always on option a), like the dialog?
owner_decisions.recommended: Natural order: drop "the recommended option first" from SKILL.md:57 and questions.md:38; keep the dialog rule.

owner_decisions.question: For prompts meant for code or agents, should the method name an environment variable (such as OPENAI_API_KEY) instead of a [[api key]] placeholder, always suggest rotating a pasted key in the first line, and never ask for a secret's value?
owner_decisions.recommended: Yes to all three.

owner_decisions.question: In image and video prompts, which details the model picks should be listed under Assumptions: every small scene detail (merged into one item), or only numbers, settings and style choices?
owner_decisions.recommended: Numbers, settings and style choices as their own items; small scene details merged into one item.

owner_decisions.question: Keep the approved cap rule (plan.md:70: cap a dimension at 3 only when it rests only on defaults) and just fix the template's sample score, or adopt a stricter rule where anything above 3 must come from what the user stated or confirmed?
owner_decisions.recommended: Keep the approved rule; set the sample to Context 3 and Output format 3, and make the sample menu show Fill placeholders ★.

owner_decisions.question: Keep the 8,000-character rule as a check on where the key sections start (and reword plan.md:82), or require whole sections to fit, which means cutting about 940 characters of method text and re-running the evals? Should quick mode also read references/questions.md, so a later deep round has the full question rules?
owner_decisions.recommended: Keep it as a start check, reword plan.md:82, and copy the caveat text and the at-most-3 caps into SKILL.md:90. Quick mode reading questions.md: your call (one extra 5.4 KB read per quick run).
owner_decisions.decision: Accepted as recommended on 2026-11-04. The second question (should quick mode also read references/questions.md?) had no recommendation and is still open.

owner_decisions.question: Will anyone but you record history fixtures, possibly on Windows? May the fix spend one billed recording (capped at $1) to confirm the skill still reads its references when Read is limited to the plugin folder?
owner_decisions.recommended: Also run the secret scan from validate.mjs either way, so every committed fixture is checked; allow the one recording.

owner_decisions.question: Add a windows-latest CI job for build --check, validate and node --test?
owner_decisions.recommended: Yes, after the fixes for 13 and 16 land.

owner_decisions.question: How should blueprint.md:56 and :99 name the patterns they warn against once the self-lint covers the references: in backticks, with the lint skipping code spans, or reworded without the literal words?
owner_decisions.recommended: Backticks, with the lint skipping code spans only (not quoted text).

owner_decisions.question: May build.mjs refuse a recording whose Read used offset or limit, so it has to be re-recorded? No committed recording has one.
owner_decisions.recommended: Yes (low stakes).

owner_decisions.question: Is claude -p close enough to a chatbot for the universal test, or should it call the Messages API directly (needs an ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, billed separately, and replaces the approach plan.md:177 approved)?
owner_decisions.recommended: Keep claude -p, add --safe-mode and --strict-mcp-config, and fail the case if the init event lists any tool or MCP server.

owner_decisions.question: Which billed eval cases should be added: a deep round, change N, Run it now, ok at the menu? Each costs about $0.10-0.20 per run plus a one-time recording. Should the universal test reuse the eval graders, including LLM-judged ones?
owner_decisions.recommended: Add deep, change N and ok-at-the-menu (after D1); keep the universal test's own regex checks.

owner_decisions.question: How should CI publish to npm? (a) Trusted publishing with a direct npm publish: fully automatic, though npm's best-practice list prefers staging. (b) Trusted publishing with npm stage publish: you approve each version with 2FA, then run the MCP Registry publish by hand. (c) Publish by hand at every release and remove npm from the workflow.
owner_decisions.recommended: (a), on Node 24.

owner_decisions.question: Split release.yml into four jobs so only the publishing jobs hold write or OIDC permissions? main has no branch protection or rulesets: protect it and limit who can create v* tags? owner_decisions.recommended: Four-job split; protect main and v* tags; refuse tags not on main; trust main's CI instead of re-running it.

owner_decisions.question: Pin the mcp-publisher download by its SHA-256, or verify its Sigstore bundle with cosign as the registry guide does?
owner_decisions.recommended: SHA-256 pin (no new action; update the hash with each version bump).

owner_decisions.question: While the stale-data issue stays open, should each run add a comment (notifies watchers) or only refresh the list? GitHub switches off scheduled workflows after 60 quiet days, the same span after which entries go stale: is a doc note enough, or should the check run weekly with a 45-day window?
owner_decisions.recommended: Comment on each run; weekly with a 45-day window (otherwise the reminder almost never fires in a quiet repository).

owner_decisions.question: Move the workflows (handoff step 2) right after 1c, before 1d, so the docs need no interim wording? ci.yml runs only on pull requests and pushes to main: may the session open a draft PR to main at step 2 so CI runs?
owner_decisions.recommended: Yes to both.

findings.title: Universal core offers "Save to file" in chat apps and never defines it
findings.summary: True on this branch. The universal core's menu line (universal/prompt-engine.md:51) lists Save to file and leaves dropping it to the model, and section 6 (lines 55-58) has no Save rule. With every tool disabled, 5 of 6 live menus today still offered it, which contradicts plan.md:74, docs/manual-checks.md:32 and universal/README.md:52. The MCP brief embeds the same text and has no overwrite rule.

claims.claim: Line 51 offers Save to file and leaves dropping it to the model's judgment.
claims.evidence: universal/prompt-engine.md:51 "3) Save to file (drop this one if you can't write files)."

claims.claim: Section 6 defines only Run it now and Refine, so picking Save to file has no rules: no path and no never-overwrite.
claims.evidence: universal/prompt-engine.md:55-58 covers Run it now (56), Refine (57) and "If the user says nothing, wait." (58). The skill's rule exists only in SKILL.md:99 ("Never overwrite an existing file"). No live universal run picked option 3, so what happens after a pick was not observed.

claims.claim: The acceptance criteria limit Save to file to Claude Code.
claims.evidence: plan.md:74 says "only offered in Claude Code and other local coding agents". That is broader than Claude Code alone, but it still excludes chat apps.

claims.claim: The docs promise that Save to file disappears in chat apps.
claims.evidence: docs/manual-checks.md:32 "'Save to file' should be missing, because chat apps can't write files." universal/README.md:52 "only appears in tools that can write files."

claims.claim: In practice the model keeps it with no tools (the reviewer cites four round-1 runs).
claims.evidence: The reviewer's run files aren't on this machine. Today's runs (Sonnet 5.5, --tools '', --strict-mcp-config): 5 of 6 menus offer Save (U2, U3 turn 2, U4 "3) Guardar en archivo", U5, U6). Only U1 dropped it.

claims.claim: Done ★ appears only under Run it now in section 6, so menus mix the two.
claims.evidence: universal/prompt-engine.md:56 "offer \"Done ★\" and say where to paste it" sits under Run it now, while line 51 shows only Run it now ★. U6 shows "1) Run it now ★ (私は画像を生成できないため…貼り付けてください)". U2 correctly showed "1) Done ★". So 1 of 2 media runs mixed the two.

claims.claim: The MCP brief embeds this core verbatim, so file-capable MCP clients get Save to file without the overwrite rule.
claims.evidence: The embedding is now at mcp/src/brief.ts:135-136; the reviewer's :90-91 refers to commit e3fd302. adaptMethod changes only the knowledge-file sentence. I built the brief and the served output-format text from a copy: line 51 appears verbatim, and /overwrite/i matches neither. One mitigation: Claude Code's own Write tool refuses to overwrite a file it hasn't read. Other hosts were not checked.

claims.claim: The universal test reported 36/36 because it only checks /What next\?/.
claims.evidence: scripts/eval/universal-test.mjs:42 checks has(/What next\?/i); docs/compatibility.md:47 says "36/36 checks passed". Also, line 26 passes --tools '' without --strict-mcp-config. claude --help (2.1.317) says --tools covers "the built-in set", so user MCP servers may still load. Not run (it would be billed).

claims.claim: The fix adds about 450 characters and keeps the contract string.
claims.evidence: Measured +392 characters (core 5,765 -> 6,157). With the finding 3 line added too, 6,459. validate.mjs passes and "Save to file" stays in the core.

findings.reproduction:
cat -n universal/prompt-engine.md -> 51: "- ### What next?: 1) Run it now ★ 2) Refine 3) Save to file (drop this one if you can't write files)."; 55-58: section 6 has Run it now, Refine and "If the user says nothing, wait." only.

git show 34d9caa:universal/prompt-engine.md | diff - universal/prompt-engine.md -> identical. git show 124b72b:universal/prompt-engine.md | sed -n 51p -> the same line. SKILL.md, output-format.md, questions.md and universal/README.md are all unchanged since 34d9caa.

Menus from today's live universal runs (every tool disabled):
  U1 "1) Run it now ★ 2) Refine"
  U2 "1) Done ★ (paste it into Midjourney, since I can't generate images) 2) Refine 3) Save to file"
  U3 turn 2 "1) Run it now ★ 2) Refine 3) Save to file"
  U4 "1) Ejecutarlo ahora ★ 2) Refinar 3) Guardar en archivo"
  U5 "1) Run it now ★ 2) Refine 3) Save to file"
  U6 "1) Run it now ★ (私は画像を生成できないため、Full promptをMidjourneyにそのまま貼り付けてください) 2) Refine 3) Save to file"
  Result: 5 of 6 offer Save.

MCP: I copied brief.ts and generated/content.ts into my folder and ran them with Node 24 type stripping. Output: 'BRIEF menu line: - ### What next?: 1) Run it now ★ 2) Refine 3) Save to file (drop this one if you can't write files).' 'BRIEF mentions overwrite: false'. 'OUTPUT-FORMAT resource mentions overwrite: false'.

The proposed no-save regex over today's outputs: FAIL for U2, U3 turn 2, U5 and U6; PASS for U1 and U4 (U4's "Guardar en archivo" gets past the English regex).

The reviewer's fix in a copy: build OK, --check OK, 'validate: OK (… 6459 chars in universal core)' (with the finding 3 line), and 31/32 script tests. The one failure is version.test.mjs, which also fails on an unpatched copy.
findings.refutation: I checked whether "drop this one if you can't write files" is enough on its own. It isn't: with no tools at all, 5 of 6 runs kept the option. I checked for a fix after 34d9caa: the core is byte-identical, and brief.ts changes since then touch only the reference adaptations. I checked whether plan.md allows Save in chat apps: it doesn't (line 74). I looked for other overwrite protection in the MCP text: there is none. Claude Code's Write tool guards against blind overwrites, but that is host behavior, not the method's. I also checked the docs' premise. "Chat apps can't write files" is too broad: the repo's own docs say Claude.ai has "Code execution and file creation" (plan.md:35, docs/install.md:59). That changes how the docs should be worded, not the defect. The harm per pick is low: picking Save was not observed, and in an app with no file tool the model would likely just say it can't.

audit.reasoning:
The defect is real on this branch. universal/prompt-engine.md:51 lists "3) Save to file (drop this one if you can't write files)", so dropping it is left to the model. Section 6 (lines 55-58) has no Save rule: it gives no path and no never-overwrite. The file is byte-identical to 34d9caa, so the defect was not fixed later.

Today's live runs had every tool disabled, plus --strict-mcp-config (confirmed in live/universal-probe.mjs:20). Five of six menus still offered Save (U2, U3 turn 2, U4 "Guardar en archivo", U5, U6); only U1 dropped it. U3 is the clearest case. In turn 3 the model says "I have no file access to your project", yet in turn 2 it had offered "3) Save to file". The models removed the parenthetical but kept the option.

This is not the owner's call. plan.md:74 already limits Save to "Claude Code and other local coding agents", and docs/manual-checks.md:32 and universal/README.md:52 promise the option is missing in chat apps.

The MCP side holds too. I built the brief from my copy: the menu line appears verbatim, and the brief has no Save rule and no overwrite rule. The served output-format resource only shows an example path, and the brief sends hosts to "section 5", not to that resource. Claude Code's Write tool blocks only blind overwrites; other hosts are unknown.

The 'Done ★' mix-up also holds: U6 shows "1) Run it now ★ (私は画像を生成できないため…)", while U2 correctly shows "1) Done ★".

What limits it: claude -p is a stand-in for chat apps, and the real apps are untested (the manual check is still pending). Picking Save was never observed. In a chat app the harm is a dead menu option, and the overwrite risk applies only to MCP hosts that can write files. So "major" may overstate it, but the defect stands.

audit.evidence_errors:
- The verifier quotes claude --help as saying --tools covers "the built-in set". The same line also says 'Use "" to disable all tools', which points the other way. Whether MCP tools load under --tools '' is unverified either way.
- "The core grows to 6,157 characters" describes the reviewer's text. The verifier's own finding-1 text gives 6,020. Its combined figure of 6,408 is right; I reproduced it.

findings.title: Secret handling sends the user back to paste the key again
findings.summary: On HEAD the method still turns a pasted key into a [[api key]] placeholder (SKILL.md:38, universal:14). Its own rules then list open placeholders, put the star on "Fill placeholders" and ask for their values before Run it now. The method never mentions environment variables or rotating the key, although 998e0c8 loosened the grader to accept OPENAI_API_KEY as "the better practice". In the two runs recorded today the model never asked for the key; it used the env var and advised rotation on its own. So the harm is latent, and the reviewer's "major" overstates it.

claims.claim: SKILL.md:38 and universal:14 turn a pasted key into [[api key]].
claims.evidence: SKILL.md:38 "Replace API keys, passwords, tokens ... with placeholders such as `[[api key]]`, and say that you did." universal/prompt-engine.md:14 "Replace secrets such as API keys with placeholders like [[api key]], and say so." `git log -L38,38` shows only 8a15447, so the line has not changed since the first commit.

arbitration.rationale:
I re-read or re-ran every fact both agents cite, and they hold. What is not settled is whether the finding's main harm is a defect at all.

The gap. Section 6 of SKILL.md (lines 95-100) and section 6 of the universal core (lines 55-58) never say what counts as a pick. They also say nothing about ok, 👍 or thanks. Every ok rule sits under a question-round heading: SKILL.md:66 (under :55), universal:33 (under :25) and questions.md:79. None of these files changed since 34d9caa.

What was observed. In U3 turn 3 the model read "ok" at the menu as Run it now. That is one run. Tools were disabled, so nothing was edited.

Why this is the owner's call:
- Arguments that ok should pick the ★: the method teaches that ok accepts the ★, and the menu has exactly one ★. README.md:67 already lets one keystroke (Enter) pick the recommended option in the Claude Code menu dialog.
- Arguments against: README.md:60 limits ok to answering questions, and README.md:62 says "`1` runs it here".
- No file and no plan.md line decides between these. If the owner wants ok to pick the ★, U3 behaved correctly and the major harm is gone.

The other half of the title, "Fill placeholders can start a run", matches the current written design:
- SKILL.md:97 and universal:56 put "ask for their values first" inside Run it now.
- plan.md:72 says the ★ "moves to 'Fill placeholders first'".
- Three recorded menus show it. Two read the option as fill, then run: spanish-quick and the committed save-to-file history. The third, secret-redaction-quick, is a prompt for the user's own coding agent, and there it read it as fill, then finish the prompt. In all three, the menu line told the user what picking it would do.
- The reviewer's fix ("runs nothing by itself") would change that design, so it needs the owner's approval too.

Claims:
- Users are taught that ok, yes or 👍 accept every ★: holds, for question rounds.
- Section 6 never says how to read ok, 👍 or thanks: holds.
- An acknowledgement can be read as Run it now: seen once (U3). Whether ok there is an acknowledgement or a pick is the owner's question.
- It "starts file edits": not checkable here. Testing it needs a billed run with tools.
- Text menus are used in Codex, Gemini CLI, Copilot, Cursor and Claude.ai: partly holds. SKILL.md:93 uses a text menu wherever AskUserQuestion isn't a tool, and the universal core and the MCP brief (brief.ts:73) always use text. I did not check each named app.
- Nothing defines Fill placeholders: true in the literal sense, but SKILL.md:97 and universal:56 describe the same step.
- The universal core has no such option: true, but not a defect. The core folds the step into Run it now, and U5 turn 2 followed it.
- There is no rule for overlapping rows: holds. One overlap was seen (secret-redaction), with no harm.
- "Untested": the menu ok has now been seen once. The repo's tests and evals still don't cover it.

Some gaps exist under either answer, all minor:
- The reply rule isn't written down.
- Fill placeholders isn't named in section 6.
- The table has no rule for overlapping rows.
- No test sends a reply to the menu.
Except for the overlap rule, how to word these depends on the owner's answer.

Why not "confirmed": the verifier's own summary says whether a bare ok should run "is the owner's call", and that answer decides whether the major defect exists. Why only medium confidence: a reader could treat the unwritten rule itself as the core defect. That would make this "confirmed (minor)" with the same questions.

findings.title: Specific values the model picks get tagged [best practice] and never appear under Assumptions
findings.summary: In all four media runs recorded today (skill and universal, Midjourney, English and Japanese), the model tagged values it picked itself as [best practice]: five pines, 三本の松の木 (three pines), a palette, footprints. In 3 of the 4 runs those values appear in no Assumption. The method does say defaults go only under Assumptions (output-format.md:64, plan.md:69). But it defines [best practice] as "something the method adds", and image-video.md:10 asks for "labelled defaults" without saying where. Writing runs mostly list their values under Assumptions already, so the problem is mainly in image prompts.

claims.claim: [best practice] is defined loosely ("something the method adds").
claims.evidence: output-format.md:62 says exactly that. But :64 adds "Defaults you chose without asking don't go here; they are listed once, under Assumptions." So a rule exists. What's missing is the line between a method rule and the value picked for it: image-video.md:117-118 ask for named light and color and for "exact numbers".

claims.claim: image-video.md:10 asks for labelled defaults without saying where the label goes.
claims.evidence: image-video.md:10 "add missing details only as labelled defaults."

claims.claim: SKILL.md:88 doesn't define the tag at all.
claims.evidence: True of SKILL.md:88 itself. But SKILL.md:45 always loads output-format.md, which defines the tag, and every trace I checked reads it.

claims.claim: Models tag values they picked themselves as best practice and leave them out of Assumptions.
claims.evidence: For media prompts in today's runs: 4 of 4 tag the model's own picks as [best practice], and 3 of 4 leave them out of Assumptions. The fourth, U6, lists them under Assumption 5. The writing runs (U1, U4, skill spanish-quick) and the save-to-file history keep the values under Assumptions.

claims.claim: The user can't see them as guesses or change them with "change N".
claims.evidence: They are labelled as practice, not as guesses, and "change N" can't reach them. But they are visible in the prompt, and Refine accepts free text (SKILL.md:98).

claims.claim: This weakens the labelled-assumptions honesty rule.
claims.evidence: Mild form only. It conflicts with plan.md:69 ("defaults appear here only") and with the no-invention standard in plan.md:172 (every number comes from the user, a placeholder or an assumption). Nothing is presented as the user's requirement, so the rule in SKILL.md:13 still holds.

claims.claim: Evidence: the save-to-file history has "Alternative titles and tags [best practice]" and also Assumption 4.
claims.evidence: The facts are right (9th line of the history file). But that is the shape the reviewer's own fix prescribes: the kind of rule tagged, its values listed under Assumptions. It shows duplication, not this defect.

claims.claim: Evidence: universal round-1 output from before d63abbf tagged skipped ★ answers as [best practice].
claims.evidence: That file is a scratch output and isn't in the repo. Today's U3 turn 2 tags the accepted ★ answers [your answer] and doesn't repeat them under Assumptions (one run).

audit.fix_corrections:
1. Don't use "five pines" (the verifier's example) or "three pines, a lantern" (the reviewer's) in the method. Both come from the cabin eval's own outputs. Models copy method wording: the save-to-file history's "[[shop name]]: the name buyers know you by" mirrors output-format.md:22. So the example could leak into the image-midjourney-quick case that is meant to test this. Use the existing example from image-video.md:118, "three gulls", or generic words.
2. Also change blueprint.md:96 "or a labelled default" to "or a default listed under Assumptions". It is the model's self-check line, and it has the same gap as image-video.md:10.

findings.summary: The method promises that `ok` or a skipped question takes the ★ (SKILL.md:62, SKILL.md:66, questions.md:70, universal/prompt-engine.md:31). No rule says the ★ must be an answer the prompt can use, and questions.md:29 encourages asking for artifacts. Today's skill run of coding-vague-asks-questions starred 'Tell me, e.g. `Next.js`…' for the stack and left the usable 'Let the agent detect it from the repo' unstarred. All 7 graders passed, so the evals don't catch this.

claims.claim: The method promises that `ok`, or skipping a question, accepts every ★.

SKILL.md:57 says the same. No rule says the ★ must be an answer. A usable domain default exists (coding.md:26: 'Whatever the repo declares'), but nothing stops the model from starring a request for information instead.

claims.evidence: questions.md:29: 'When the user has an artifact, ask for it instead of a description: "Paste the error message", "Share a paragraph in the voice you want".'

The binary also has an extended schema with `kind:"text"` questions. It is switched on only by `if(D&&i.CLAUDE_CODE_QUESTION_EXTENDED)lPs(!0)` for some entrypoints. Which hosts set that: not checkable here.

findings.refutation: I looked for a rule that already makes the ★ usable. SKILL.md:57 says 'concrete options', SKILL.md:66 assumes the ★ is an answer, and coding.md:26 gives a usable stack default. None of them forbids starring a request, and today's run did it anyway. The model's slip was reasoning from the empty eval workspace ('The workspace is empty, so I can't read your stack'). audit.reasoning:
The defect is real and unchanged since 34d9caa (git diff of skills, universal, README.md, evals and plan.md is empty). The method promises that `ok` and skipped questions take the ★, and that each accepted ★ is used 'as offered' (SKILL.md:62, :66; questions.md:70; universal/prompt-engine.md:31, :33). No general rule says the ★ must work as an answer: questions.md:35-40, SKILL.md:57 and universal:26 ask only for concrete options and a reason. The closest rule is coding.md:17 ('★ marks the recommended default, used when the user replies `ok`'). But it describes the pack's table, not the options the model writes, and the failing run read coding.md anyway. The raw trace /private/tmp/e-7HBxcP/out/trace.jsonl shows 'a) Tell me, e.g. `Next.js`, `React + Express`, `Django` ★' with 'b) Let the agent detect it from the repo' unstarred, and the message ends with the `ok` line.

I tried three refutations, and none holds.
1. 'Concrete options' could be read as banning a request. The model didn't read it that way, and questions.md:29 invites artifact requests without saying where they go.
2. It could be an artifact of the empty eval workspace. But chat apps have no repo either. U3 handled it ('Detect it from the repo ★'); the skill run didn't.
3. The MCP path has the same hole, from code reading (no run). ask_user preselects the ★ in the form (mcp/src/questions.ts:244). A form submitted unchanged returns it as source 'chosen' (questions.ts:273), and a decline returns the ★ answers (mcp/src/server.ts:281-283). So a 'Tell me' ★ would come back as the user's answer.

Secondary claims:
- The dialog claim mostly holds. The standard schema needs 2-4 options and adds 'Other' automatically. A text-question kind exists only behind CLAUDE_CODE_QUESTION_EXTENDED, and only for SDK, desktop, local-agent and remote entrypoints, not the terminal CLI.
- What the model does after `ok` is not checkable without a billed run. SKILL.md:75 allows a [[placeholder]], so 'has to guess or ask again' is overstated.
- The other two live skill rounds starred usable answers. critique-1 Q5 already shows the wanted pattern: a usable ★ plus '(You can paste a paragraph in your brand's voice instead.)'.

findings.title: Language rules conflict with the media rule, and the files disagree on translating headings
findings.summary: There are two separate problems, and neither has changed since 34d9caa. (1) SKILL.md:36, blueprint.md:103 and universal:12 ask for a reply-language line with no exception for image or video prompts, and the universal core lacks image-video.md:126's rule (ask, or keep the user's language and list it as an assumption). (2) output-format.md:3 says to translate the headings, but the universal core says nothing about it. Today's non-English runs disagree: three kept English headings with mixed-language menus, and one (U4) translated everything.

audit.reasoning:
Both halves exist on this branch and are unchanged since 34d9caa.

The language line:
- SKILL.md:36 and universal:12 ask for 'a line telling the target model which language to answer in', and blueprint.md:103 checks for it. None has a media exception. blueprint.md:3 exempts media only from the skeleton.
- plan.md:52 says the same ('adding a "Respond in <language>" line'), while plan.md:62 wants media prompts in 'the target tool's own format'. The fix reconciles two plan lines; it doesn't override a decision.
- In the skill the conflict is on paper only. image-video.md:126 governs media language, and no media prompt in today's runs has a language line (skill English and Japanese Midjourney, U2, U6).
- The universal core is the real gap. 'translate silently' appears 0 times in universal/prompt-engine.md; it is only in the optional knowledge file (line 697). In U6 a Japanese request became an English prompt. The reply said so, but it justified the switch with an unverified claim tagged [best practice] ('Midjourneyは英語の方が認識精度が高い'). It didn't list the choice under Assumptions. So 'silent' is overstated, but 'not offered as a changeable choice' holds.

Headings:
- The files don't really disagree. output-format.md:3 says 'Use the headings below in the user's language'. The universal core is silent, and its 'reply in the user's language' (universal:12) points the same way.
- The real problem is behavior. Both skill runs read output-format.md and still kept English headings and English menu labels with translated text (raw traces e-Z6c1eS and e-x3sLM8). U6 did the same, while U4 translated everything, down to 'cambia 2: …'.

findings.title: The description promises "critique", but there is no critique path
findings.summary: The facts hold. The description says 'improve, critique or write' (SKILL.md:3), but nothing in the skill body, the universal core, the MCP server or plan.md says what a critique request gets. In two live runs, 'What's missing from this prompt?' got one or two sentences listing the gaps, then a round of 7 or 5 questions. So, unlike the finding says, the user does get a short direct answer. Whether a feedback-only request needs its own path, or 'critique' should leave the description, is a product-scope choice.

claims.claim: The description triggers on 'critique'.
claims.evidence: SKILL.md:3 'Use to improve, critique or write a prompt ...'. git log -L3,3 shows it arrived in 55a5b2b, 'Tune the skill description ...'.

claims.claim: The body covers only improving and writing prompts.
claims.evidence: SKILL.md:19 covers 'improve, enhance, rewrite, expand or optimize a prompt', a prompt for another AI tool, or invocation by name. Outside generated files, git grep -i critique finds only SKILL.md:3. universal/prompt-engine.md:9 ('improve, rewrite or write'), mcp/src/server.ts:63 and :213, and plan.md:51 (the trigger list) don't mention it either.

findings.title: build.mjs does nothing, silently, when its path has a space, goes through a symlink, or is on Windows
findings.summary: scripts/build.mjs:205 runs main() only when import.meta.url equals `file://${process.argv[1]}`. On this Mac, `build.mjs --check` exits 0 with no output on a stale tree, and `build.mjs` writes nothing, in three cases: a folder whose name has a space or a non-ASCII letter, a path through a symlink, and a path under /tmp. This causes the one failing root test here (version.test.mjs). CI is not affected, because it runs on ubuntu-latest, where checkout paths have no spaces or symlinks.

claims.claim: The guard compares import.meta.url with `file://${process.argv[1]}`.
claims.evidence: scripts/build.mjs:205: "if (import.meta.url === `file://${process.argv[1]}`) main();". build.mjs is unchanged since 34d9caa (`git log 34d9caa..HEAD -- scripts/build.mjs` is empty).

claims.claim: import.meta.url is percent-encoded and is the real path; argv[1] is neither, so they differ for spaces, non-ASCII names and symlinks.
claims.evidence: A probe printed both sides. Space: 'with%20space' vs 'with space'. Accent: 'caf%C3%A9' vs 'café'. Symlink: '.../symtarget/...' vs '.../symlink/...'. /tmp: 'file:///private/tmp/...' vs 'file:///tmp/...'. All four print equal: false; the plain real-path copy prints true. Node resolves argv[1] to an absolute path but does not follow symlinks.

claims.claim: On Windows the guard can never match.
claims.evidence: No Windows machine here. A simulation supports the claim: Node's pathToFileURL('C:\\Users\\dev\\prompt-engine\\scripts\\build.mjs', {windows:true}) gives 'file:///C:/Users/dev/prompt-engine/scripts/build.mjs', while the guard builds 'file://C:\\Users\\dev\\prompt-engine\\scripts\\build.mjs'.

claims.claim: When they differ, build.mjs writes nothing, and --check exits 0 with no output even on a stale tree.
claims.evidence: Reproduced in four copies: a folder with a space, a symlink, a non-ASCII folder, and a /tmp path. In each, after media-targets.md was made stale, `--check` exited 0 and printed nothing, and `build` exited 0 but left the stale line in place.

claims.claim: validate.mjs reports the file stale and says to run build.mjs, but running it does nothing.
claims.evidence: scripts/validate.mjs:217. In the copy with a space it printed 'error: skills/prompt-engine/references/media-targets.md: stale; run node scripts/build.mjs' and exited 1. Running build.mjs afterwards left the file unchanged.

claims.claim: version.mjs:73 runs build.mjs this way, so a version bump can leave mcp/src/generated/content.ts with the old VERSION.
claims.evidence: Holds whenever the real path has a space or a non-ASCII letter. In '$W/bump space/repo', `version.mjs 9.8.7` exited 0, but content.ts:4 still read 'export const VERSION = "0.1.0";'. Through a symlink it fails only when PE_ROOT names the symlinked path, as the test sets it. Without PE_ROOT, `root` comes from import.meta.url (build.mjs:16), which is already a real path, so the bump worked (VERSION "9.8.7").

claims.claim: On macOS os.tmpdir() is under /var, a symlink to /private/var, so the version test fails.
claims.evidence: os.tmpdir() = /var/folders/6w/.../T, and /var -> private/var. Today the failing test is the second one, not the first: commit 5beff3a added a test before it. The failure reads 'sets the version everywhere and the repository still validates ... error: mcp/src/generated/content.ts: stale'. The test passes with TMPDIR set to a real folder and fails with TMPDIR set through /tmp.

claims.claim: (Extra) `npm run generate` in mcp/ uses the same entry point.
claims.evidence: mcp/package.json:40 has '"generate": "node ../scripts/build.mjs"', so the same guard applies. I did not run it separately from a path with a space. Run from mcp/ with a relative ../ path in a real-path folder, both the old and the fixed guard work.

findings.reproduction:
$W = <scratch>/work/verify-scripts-build. Each copy was made with `git archive HEAD | tar -x`. I appended a line to skills/prompt-engine/references/media-targets.md, then ran from /:
- $W/plain/repo (control): `--check` exit=1, printing 'stale: skills/prompt-engine/references/media-targets.md'. `build` printed 'wrote ...'. validate OK.
- "$W/with space/repo", $W/symlink/repo (a link to $W/symtarget), $W/café/repo, and /tmp/claude-502/.../plain/repo: `--check` exit=0 with no output. `build` exit=0, and the stale line was still there (count 1). validate: 'error: skills/prompt-engine/references/media-targets.md: stale; run node scripts/build.mjs', '1 error(s)'.
- Version bump in "$W/bump space/repo": `node scripts/version.mjs 9.8.7` printed '... → 9.8.7' for 6 files, then 'Then run the checks and tag v9.8.7', exit=0. content.ts:4 still read 'export const VERSION = "0.1.0";'. validate: 'error: mcp/src/generated/content.ts: stale'.

With TMPDIR=$W/realtmp: pass 4, fail 0. With TMPDIR=/tmp/.../realtmp: fail 1. `git status` stayed empty.

findings.refutation: I looked for a fix after 34d9caa and found none: build.mjs and version.mjs are unchanged. I checked whether CI would hit it. It doesn't: ci.yml:14 runs on ubuntu-latest, where checkout paths have no spaces or symlinks and /tmp is a real folder. I checked whether a stale file could get past the full check sequence. It can't: validate.mjs:216-217 compares buildAll() with the files on disk, independent of the guard, and mcp/test/brief.test.ts:240-244 requires 'generated files are up to date' in the output, so that test fails rather than passing silently. The owner's checkout (<repo>) is a real path without spaces, so the normal workflow works. I also ruled out another cause for the macOS test failure: the same test passes with a real TMPDIR. What remains is real: `--check` gives a false pass on its own; build.mjs, version.mjs and `npm run generate` silently do nothing; validate's advice doesn't help; and a required check fails on macOS.

audit.reasoning: scripts/build.mjs:205 compares import.meta.url with 'file://' + process.argv[1]. import.meta.url is the real path and is percent-encoded; argv[1] is neither. findings.title: The history sanitizer writes API keys, tokens, home paths, hostnames and session IDs into fixtures meant for a public repo
findings.summary: True on this branch. sanitize() keeps the conversation word for word. It rewrites only the exact plugin and temp-folder paths, and its only check is a refusal of ASCII-domain e-mails. So keys, tokens, other home paths, hostnames and the session ID in a recording pass straight through. Windows paths are never rewritten, npm specs such as next-auth@5.0.0 are refused without saying where, CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR is ignored, and no test can import the module. The three committed fixtures are clean, so the risk is in future recordings.

claims.claim: sanitize() keeps message, toolUseResult and thinking word for word, rewrites only the exact repo and cwd strings, and its only scan is an ASCII e-mail regex.
claims.evidence: record-history.mjs:70 KEEP_KEYS includes 'message' and 'toolUseResult'; :75 copies the values as they are; :82 text.split(repo).join('/plugin').split(cwd).join('/workspace'); :83 /[\w.+-]+@[\w-]+\.[\w.-]+/. The file is unchanged since 34d9caa (git diff empty; last change 998e0c8).

claims.claim: Other private data in the first message, assistant text, thinking and anything the Read tool opens is written to the fixture.
claims.evidence: Run A (fake claude, planted transcript) exited 0 and out.jsonl kept everything planted. From the first message: an sk-ant key, a ghp_ token and an AKIA key. From a thinking block: /Users/alice, a foreign hostname, this Mac's hostname, the original session UUID and a claude.ai session_ URL. From a Read of a home file: its path, an sk-proj key and jürgen@müller.de. Also msg_ IDs. Only the attachment event's e-mail and an api-request-blob event were dropped. Context: thinking text is empty in the committed fixtures and in today's 2.1.317 transcript (signature only). The permissions doc says a bare tool name matches all uses of the tool, so the recorder's --allowedTools Read (line 37) pre-approves reads outside the working folder.

claims.claim: (a) The path rewrite runs on serialized JSON, so Windows paths are never rewritten.
claims.evidence: With sanitize() copied verbatim from HEAD, repo C:\Users\alice\src\prompt-engine and a Temp cwd both come out unchanged; POSIX paths come out as /plugin/... and /workspace. JSON doubles the backslashes, so split(repo) can never match. I could not run it on Windows. The fixture would also stay stale, because build.mjs:137 refreshes Reads only under ^/plugin/. Scope: no doc claims Windows support for maintainers, and the parked CI runs only on ubuntu.

claims.claim: (b) The e-mail regex refuses package specs without saying where, yet misses non-ASCII addresses.
claims.evidence: Refused: next-auth@5.0.0, @modelcontextprotocol/sdk@1.2.3, @anthropic-ai/claude-code@2.1.312 and git@github.com:… . The message ('sanitized transcript still contains an e-mail-like string; refusing to write it') names no line or text. In run B the refusal came after the (fake) model call. Missed: jürgen@müller.de and ivan@пример.рф, which have non-ASCII domains. Still caught: jürgen@example.com, through its ASCII tail. So only non-ASCII domains slip through.

claims.claim: (c) The transcript is looked for only in ~/.claude/projects, ignoring CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, and only after the billed call.
claims.evidence: Line 49 is const projects = join(homedir(), '.claude', 'projects'), and it runs after the spawn at :33. The sessions doc says CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR will 'Move storage off ~/.claude'. The env-vars doc says 'All settings, session history, and plugins are stored under this path', and that the variable can also be set in user or managed settings. Run C1 made one call, then failed with 'transcript for session … not found under <W>/home/.claude/projects'. Run C2, with no ~/.claude, failed with 'ENOENT … scandir …/.claude/projects'. The real claude wasn't run (billed); the fake writes where the docs say.

claims.claim: (d) Importing the module runs the recorder, so sanitize() has no tests.
claims.evidence: Importing prints the usage text and exits 2, because lines 20-24 run at import. A node:test file that imports it reports 'fail 1 … test failed'. No file in scripts/test mentions record-history or sanitize.

claims.claim: The three committed fixtures are clean, and the type filter drops the attachment events that hold the account e-mail.
claims.evidence: I scanned all three evals/*/history.jsonl. They contain no '@' at all, no /Users or /home path, no key or token pattern, no session_ URL, no /private, /var/folders or /tmp path, and no UUID other than event IDs and the fixed session ID. They do keep msg_ IDs (8, 8 and 6) and toolu_ IDs. Line 62 keeps only user and assistant events. In today's real 2.1.317 transcript, account and environment context sits in attachment events (session_context, environment).

claims.claim: Reviewer's evidence: the proposed patterns find nothing in the fixtures and catch every planted item.
claims.evidence: They find nothing in the three fixtures, and they catch the planted keys, token, /Users path, session URL and non-ASCII e-mail. The scan alone misses hostnames and the session UUID. Fix (2) handles this machine's hostname and the session ID, but in my prototype of the reviewer's fix a foreign hostname (alice-mbp.corp.internal) still got through.

claims.claim: Severity is major.
claims.evidence: The gaps are real and the output is public. But the input is mostly the maintainer's own, today's fixtures are clean, thinking text is currently empty, and CONTRIBUTING.md:109 asks for a manual read. The same sentence overstates what the script does. I rate it minor.

findings.refutation: Checked for a later fix: git diff 34d9caa HEAD -- scripts/eval/record-history.mjs is empty. Checked whether real recordings put private data in the kept events. Today's followup eval left a gitignored 2.1.317 transcript in evals/followup-ok-accepts-recommendations/. In it, account and environment context sits only in attachment events, which line 62 drops. The kept events hold the first message, the skill text, Read calls and results, and assistant text, and the thinking text is empty. So on macOS and Linux a default recording is clean unless the message, a Read result or the model's own text carries private data. That lowers the likelihood; it doesn't close the gap. The hostnames, session URL and original session ID were planted; I know of no path that puts them into a normal recording. Reads of private files are allowed by the flags (per the docs), but I didn't test it with a real model. I couldn't run the Windows case on Windows; it follows from the code. CONTRIBUTING.md:109 asks for a manual read, which is a real safeguard, but the same sentence overstates what the script does. plan.md has no decision about fixture privacy. The raw transcript the eval left in evals/ is not from this script: .gitignore:9-10 keeps it out of git, and release.mjs zips only skills/prompt-engine. Net: the defect stands, and I lowered the severity to minor.

audit.reasoning:
I reach the same verdict and the same severity (minor). scripts/eval/record-history.mjs has not changed since 998e0c8, and the diff from 34d9caa is empty. sanitize() copies message and toolUseResult as they are (:70, :75). It rewrites only the repo and temp-folder strings, and only in the serialized JSON (:82). Its only check is an ASCII e-mail regex (:83).

I reproduced every sub-claim in my own copy, using a fake claude:
- Planted keys, a token, a foreign /Users path, jürgen@müller.de and a session URL are all written to the output.
- Windows paths are not rewritten, with either separator.
- next-auth@5.0.0, @scope/pkg@1.2.3 and git@github.com are refused after the call, and the error doesn't say where the match is.
- CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR is ignored.
- Importing the module exits 2.

Real data narrows the risk:
- I ran HEAD's sanitize() over two transcripts from today's `claude -p --plugin-dir` critique runs. These used Claude Code 2.1.317 and the owner's real config and account. The output has no e-mail, home path, username, hostname or original session ID. The account e-mail appears only in session_context and remote_session_change attachments and in api-request-blob events. Line 62 drops all of those.
- The thinking text is empty in all 7 real transcripts. The thinking doc says display "defaults to \"omitted\"" on Claude 5 and later models.
- A secret typed in the first message does survive. I ran sanitize() over today's secret-redaction-quick eval transcript. The repo's fake key stays three times: in the first message, in the Skill call's args, and in the skill text's "ARGUMENTS:" line. The model's reply had redacted it.

So a normal macOS recording is clean today. A leak needs one of these: private data in the maintainer's first message, a Read outside the plugin folder, visible thinking from an older model, or a recording made on Windows. Per the permissions doc, the bare Read at :37 pre-approves reads outside the plugin folder. That fits minor, not major.

This isn't an owner decision:
- .claude/CLAUDE.md step 1 already lists the sanitizer as likely high value. Its wording "only redacts" is off: the script refuses, it doesn't redact.
- plan.md says nothing about fixtures.
- The Windows, config-folder and false-refusal bugs are plain defects.

One fact is sharper than the verifier stated. If a script run with two arguments imports this module, the import runs a whole recording. With the real binary, that is a billed call, and it writes a file.

findings.title: refreshHistory finds the skill body by guesswork, which can corrupt or freeze the recorded skill text without failing any check
findings.summary: refreshHistory finds the old skill body by searching. It starts at the first '\n# ' (build.mjs:146) and ends at the last 'ARGUMENTS:' (build.mjs:147). The three committed recordings are refreshed exactly today, because each has an ARGUMENTS line. Three inputs corrupt or freeze a fixture with no check failing: a recording made without arguments, a SKILL.md body with no H1, and arguments that contain 'ARGUMENTS:'. Text placed before the H1 grows by one copy on every build, but that case is loud.

claims.claim: Claude Code appends the ARGUMENTS line only when there are arguments (installed 2.1.317).
claims.evidence: The binary has 'e=e.replaceAll("$ARGUMENTS",()=>(Z=!0,w(n))),!Z&&r&&n)e=e+`\n\nARGUMENTS: ${w(n)}`' inside 'function _Ve(e,n,r=!0,s=[],h,y)'. Plugin skills call it as '_Ve(Lo,Zn,!0,Ve,...)', where Lo starts with 'Base directory for this skill: '. So the line is added when the arguments are non-empty and no placeholder was substituted.

claims.claim: The reviewer's quote from the 2.1.312 bundle.
claims.evidence: Only 2.1.317 is installed. `npm view @anthropic-ai/claude-code@2.1.312 dist.unpackedSize` = 190085, so the npm package is a wrapper and the code ships in a platform binary. The committed recordings, made with 2.1.312 according to the review, have the same shape as 2.1.317's.

claims.claim: SKILL.md:34 itself contains `ARGUMENTS:`.
claims.evidence: skills/prompt-engine/SKILL.md:34: '...arrives on a line that starts with `ARGUMENTS:`.' Every committed and live skill text contains 'ARGUMENTS:' twice.

claims.claim: (a) With a recording made without arguments, the new body is spliced in front of the stale tail of the old one. Later builds don't change it, and the checks pass.

claims.claim: (b) Text before SKILL.md's H1 is copied again on every build, and the checks never pass.

claims.claim: (c) If the body has no H1, the refresh is skipped from then on, silently.

claims.claim: In all three cases the follow-up evals test something other than the current SKILL.md.
claims.evidence: True for (a) and (c). In (b) the checks fail, so it can't pass the gate unnoticed.

The candidate (verify-scripts-build/fixes/candidate-refresh.mjs) leaves the committed fixtures byte-identical. But its strict check, text.endsWith('

ARGUMENTS: ' + args), can reject valid recordings. In 2.1.317, plugin-skill arguments go through c0, which rewrites '(^|\s)!' to '$1\!', '!`' to '! `' and '`!' to '` !', and through unn, which substitutes ${CLAUDE_*} variables. I did not check at runtime whether the escape survives into the transcript. Safer: when the recorded arguments are non-empty, cut at the last '

ARGUMENTS: ' and throw only if there is none; when they are empty, cut nothing. The body's own 'ARGUMENTS:' at SKILL.md:34 follows a backtick, not a blank line. findings.title: Ordinary Windows and macOS checkouts fail every check: CRLF line endings and Finder's .DS_Store files
findings.summary: Git for Windows' default install sets core.autocrlf=true, which gives a CRLF checkout. On one, validate fails with 8 misleading errors, build --check reports 6 stale files, 6 of 32 script tests fail and version.mjs refuses to run. The fix the error text suggests, running build.mjs, makes it worse: content.ts and the three history.jsonl files get `\r\n` in their text, and every further build run adds another copy of the SKILL.md frontmatter to each history.jsonl. On macOS, a Finder .DS_Store in the skill folder or references/ fails validate, release.mjs and the 'repository passes as-is' test. Nothing that ships to users is affected.

claims.claim: There is no .gitattributes.
claims.evidence: `git ls-files | grep -i gitattributes` and `git log --all -- .gitattributes '**/.gitattributes'` both return nothing. There is none on disk either.

claims.claim: The scripts only handle LF: the frontmatter regexes at validate.mjs:33, build.mjs:168 and version.mjs:65, and the generated-file comparisons.
claims.evidence:
validate.mjs:33 `/^---
([\s\S]*?)
---
?/`, build.mjs:168 `/^---
[\s\S]*?
---
/` and version.mjs:65 use the same LF-only pattern. validate.mjs:217 and build.mjs:194 compare the raw file text.

claims.claim: On a CRLF checkout, validate gives 8 errors: missing YAML frontmatter, '### 5. Present' at char 8247, and 6 stale files.
claims.evidence: Reproduced exactly in a clone made with core.autocrlf=true.

claims.claim: build --check prints 6 stale lines.
claims.evidence: Reproduced: media-targets.md, the knowledge file, the 3 history.jsonl files and content.ts.

claims.claim: `node scripts/version.mjs 0.1.1` fails with 'no metadata.version line in the frontmatter'.
claims.evidence: On a real CRLF checkout it fails earlier, at the lockfile: 'mcp/package-lock.json: unexpected formatting; run `npm version 0.1.1 --no-git-tag-version` in mcp/ instead'. That hint is misleading. The SKILL.md message only appears once the lockfile is LF. Neither case writes anything (git status stays clean).

claims.claim: Ordinary Windows checkouts get CRLF.
claims.evidence: In git-for-windows/build-extra installer/install.iss (fetched today with gh api), lines 2373-2379 preselect 'CRLFAlways'. Lines 3262-3267 then write core.autocrlf=true.

claims.claim: Ordinary Windows and macOS checkouts fail every check.
claims.evidence: Overstated. `claude plugin validate . --strict` passes on the CRLF clone. A macOS checkout only fails once Finder writes a .DS_Store, and then build --check still passes. Only validate, release.mjs and one test fail.

claims.claim: With a .DS_Store present: walk() (validate.mjs:89) and the reference listing (validate.mjs:143) include it and validate fails. It is gitignored (.gitignore:7) and left out of the zip (release.mjs:36), but release.mjs runs validate first (release.mjs:30), so the release fails too.
claims.evidence: Reproduced: 3 errors. release.mjs --zip stops at 'Command failed: node scripts/validate.mjs' and creates no dist/. In scripts/test/validate.test.mjs, 'the repository passes as-is' also fails, because copyRepo copies .DS_Store.

claims.claim: New, not in the review: running build.mjs on a CRLF checkout corrupts the generated files.
claims.evidence: After `node scripts/build.mjs`, git diff shows real content changes in content.ts (every string gains `\r\n`) and in the 3 history.jsonl files. Each further run adds one frontmatter copy to each history.jsonl: 69,348 → 69,747 → 70,146 bytes, and 1 → 2 → 3 copies (HEAD has 0). Cause: build.mjs:168 fails to strip the frontmatter, then build.mjs:146 splices the body in again after the first '\n# '.

findings.refutation: None of the cited files has changed since 34d9caa (`git log 34d9caa..HEAD` on the scripts, .gitignore and data). I checked whether CRLF checkouts are realistic: Git for Windows defaults to autocrlf=true. I checked whether the CRLF failure is only cosmetic: it isn't, because following the hint writes wrong content. I checked who is affected. CI runs only on ubuntu-latest (pending-workflows/ci.yml:14, :35) and isn't active yet, so CI isn't affected. Claude Code's own validator accepts CRLF. .DS_Store never ships, because it is gitignored and left out of the zip. No doc promises Windows support for contributors. The finding overstates 'every check' and 'ordinary macOS checkouts', but the core defect holds. It rates major because a Windows contributor can't get one check to pass, and the suggested fix damages eval fixtures.

audit.reasoning:
The core defect reproduces on this branch. I cloned a repo built from `git archive HEAD` with core.autocrlf=true, which gave 198 files with CRLF and the 2 PNGs as binary. On that clone, validate gives the same 8 errors: missing frontmatter, '### 5. Present' at char 8247, and 6 stale files. build --check lists the same 6 files. `version.mjs 0.1.1` stops at the lockfile message. With the lockfile converted to LF it stops at 'no metadata.version line'. Neither run writes anything.

Running build.mjs three times grows evals/save-to-file/history.jsonl from 68,235 to 69,348, 69,747 and 70,146 bytes. That is 1, 2, then 3 frontmatter copies, against 0 at HEAD. content.ts also gains `\r\n` inside its strings.

A .DS_Store in skills/prompt-engine/ and references/ gives 3 validate errors. It also stops `release.mjs --zip` before dist/ exists and fails 'the repository passes as-is'. A .DS_Store at the root or in evals/ is harmless.

The macOS case hits the owner's own documented step: docs/publishing.md:48 runs `node scripts/release.mjs` locally.

Git for Windows does default to CRLF. Its installer preselects CRLFAlways (install.iss:2374-2379) and writes core.autocrlf=true (:3262-3267).

There is no .gitattributes in the tree, in the history or in the global config. No cited file has changed since 34d9caa.

'Every check' is overstated: `claude plugin validate . --strict` passes on the CRLF clone and on the .DS_Store copy.
audit.checks_run:
Work folder: <scratch>/work/audit-scripts-validate.
- Read the scripts and .gitignore.
- Made src/ from `git archive HEAD`, committed it there, and cloned it with `-c core.autocrlf=true` into crlf/. Checked `git ls-files --eol`.
- In crlf/, ran validate, build --check, all script tests (TAP reporter), version.mjs 0.1.1 (also with an LF lockfile) and claude plugin validate.
- Ran build.mjs 3 times in a copy and measured the size and frontmatter count of history.jsonl.
- Ran the same tests on an LF copy (repo/) to compare.
- Simulated the Windows main-guard comparison with `pathToFileURL(path, {windows:true})`.
- .DS_Store copy (ds/): ran validate, build --check, release --zip, validate.test.mjs and plugin validate.
- Fetched installer/install.iss with a read-only gh api call and grepped for CRLFAlways.
- Looked for .gitattributes everywhere, and for .DS_Store in the real repo (none).
- Applied the proposed fix (tools/patch16.mjs) to LF, CRLF and junk-file copies.
- Cloned a repo that has the .gitattributes (crlf-ga/) and ran `git add --renormalize`.
- Probed the BOM regex forms.
- Ran all corrected fixes together on an LF copy and an all-CRLF copy (all/, all-crlf/).
audit.evidence_errors:
1. '6 of 32 script tests fail': on this Mac, test 30 ('sets the version everywhere…') also fails on a plain LF copy. That is finding 13: content.ts goes stale through the symlinked tmpdir. CRLF adds 5 failures (tests 16, 18, 19, 20 and 28), not 6.
2. The summary presents macOS results as what a Git for Windows checkout gets. On native Windows, build.mjs's main() never runs (finding 13). There import.meta.url is file:///C:/… while the guard builds file://C:\…. I simulated this from the path formats; I could not run it on Windows. So on Windows, `build.mjs --check` prints nothing and exits 0 instead of listing 6 stale files, and `node scripts/build.mjs` writes nothing. The corruption from following the hint therefore needs a CRLF tree where main() does run: macOS, Linux, or WSL over a Windows checkout. validate.mjs and version.mjs don't use that guard, so their failures do apply on Windows.
audit.fix_corrections:
1. Write the BOM regex as `/^﻿/`. The reviewer's text in findings/16.json has a literal U+FEFF there. Don't use the `\u{FEFF}` form from the CLAUDE.md gotcha: without the `u` flag, `/^\u{FEFF}/` matches the text 'u{FEFF}' and strips nothing (tested). Check the bytes after editing.
2. Land this before finding 13's main-guard fix, or with it. Once build.mjs runs on Windows, a CRLF checkout without this fix duplicates the frontmatter in history.jsonl and puts `\r\n` into content.ts.
3. The OS_JUNK filter and the release.mjs:36 `-x` additions must land together. With only today's `-x '*.DS_Store'`, Thumbs.db and desktop.ini in the skill folder go into the zip (4 junk entries in my test).
4. Tested and fine:
- The .gitattributes: an autocrlf=true clone gets 199 LF files and 2 binary; `git add --renormalize .` changes nothing.
- normalize at build.mjs:17 and :194, validate.mjs:22, and version.mjs:33, :53 and :64. With it, version.mjs 0.1.1 on the CRLF copy changes only the version lines.
- All corrected fixes together, on an LF copy and on an all-CRLF copy: build --check, validate, 31/32 tests (test 30 is finding 13), plugin validate, and release --zip (12 entries).

findings.fix_assessment:
The .gitattributes (`* text=auto eol=lf`, `*.png binary`) is correct and enough for Git checkouts. Tested: an autocrlf=true clone of a repo that has it is LF everywhere (199 w/lf, 2 w/-text). Validate, build --check, the tests and claude plugin validate all pass there. The index is already all LF with no CR or BOM, so no renormalize commit is needed, and .gitattributes isn't a forbidden root file.

The read normalization is incomplete as written. It fixes validate, but build --check still reports 6 stale files, because build.mjs:194 compares raw readFileSync output. With :194 normalized too, a CRLF clone without .gitattributes passes validate, build --check and 28/28 validate and lint tests. version.mjs 0.1.1 then changes only the version lines. It is worth keeping as a second layer, for files an editor saves with CRLF.

The OS_JUNK filter and the zip exclusions are correct. I tested them with .DS_Store, Thumbs.db and desktop.ini: validate passes, and the zip has the same 12 entries with no junk.

The reviewer's fix leaves out .gitignore lines for Thumbs.db and desktop.ini, and tests. All five fixes applied together pass every check.
findings.proposed_fix:
1. Add /.gitattributes with two lines: `* text=auto eol=lf` and `*.png binary`.
2. scripts/build.mjs: add `export const normalize = (s) => s.replace(/^﻿/, '').replace(/\r\n/g, '\n');`. Use it in read (line 17) and in main()'s comparison (line 194). Import it in scripts/validate.mjs (line 22) and scripts/version.mjs (lines 33, 53, 64) and wrap those readFileSync calls. Leave release.mjs:59 alone: it hashes binary files.
3. scripts/validate.mjs: add `const OS_JUNK = new Set(['.DS_Store', 'Thumbs.db', 'desktop.ini']);`. Add `.filter((f) => !OS_JUNK.has(f))` in walk() (line 89) and to refFiles (line 143).
4. scripts/release.mjs:36: `'-x', '*.DS_Store', '*Thumbs.db', '*desktop.ini'`.
5. .gitignore: add `Thumbs.db` and `desktop.ini` after line 7.
6. scripts/test/validate.test.mjs: add 'passes with CRLF line endings', which converts SKILL.md and references/media-targets.md to CRLF and expects exit 0. Add 'ignores .DS_Store in the skill folder', which writes references/.DS_Store and expects exit 0.
owner_questions: Optional: should CI also run the root checks (build --check, validate, node --test) on windows-latest? Without that, nothing stops Windows support from breaking again. release.mjs needs zip and unzip, so it would stay Linux-only.

Optional: add a windows-latest CI job for the root checks? Until finding 13 is fixed, it would give a false pass on build --check. release.mjs --zip needs zip and unzip, so the job would cover only build --check, validate and node --test.

findings.title: The self-lint never checks the reference files, which the model reads as instructions
findings.summary: The selfCheck lint runs only on SKILL.md and universal/prompt-engine.md (validate.mjs:121). The 9 reference files are never linted, although the skill reads them in its first turn and build.mjs copies them into the knowledge file and the MCP content. CONTRIBUTING.md:48-50 and .claude/CLAUDE.md:16 both say the validator enforces this for method text. Today's references are clean, apart from two lines in blueprint.md that name the patterns in order to warn against them.

claims.claim: The 9 reference files are never checked.

findings.title: A new reference file can ship only in the skill, because nothing checks KNOWLEDGE_ORDER
findings.summary: build.mjs builds the universal knowledge file and the MCP content only from the hard-coded KNOWLEDGE_ORDER list (build.mjs:54-57). validate.mjs checks that each reference is linked from SKILL.md (:141-148), but not that it's on that list. A new reference added without CONTRIBUTING step 3 ships in the skill but not in the universal or MCP formats, and every script check passes. Even with step 3 done, the MCP server won't serve a new domain unless its hard-coded domain lists are updated, and nothing checks that either.

The header comment at validate.test.mjs:3 gives "node --test scripts/test/", which fails on Node 24 here and, per Node's docs, on every version from 21.0.0. CI and the docs use the glob form, which works.
