Confirmed that validate.mjs lints only SKILL.md and universal/prompt-engine.md (validate.mjs:120), so workflow and doc edits can't trip the lint rules or budgets.
audit.evidence_errors: No wrong lines or outputs. It leaves out facts that bear on the verdict: publishing.md:37-51 (full local checks before tagging), CLAUDE.md step 5 and plan.md:188 (Claude asks before any tag), the single collaborator, and plan.md:134 (a Node 20 and 22 boot check planned for the release tooling).
audit.fix_corrections: If the owner wants gating, the tested diff works: it parses, and I checked the on-main logic live, including the 'behind' case. Improvements: 1. Put the on-main check in its own small job that runs before `ci`, so a wrong tag fails in seconds, not after the full CI. 2. The compare API returns 404 for an annotated tag's object SHA. On git/git v2.47.0, the tag object SHA gives 404 and the tag name gives 'behind'. So if GITHUB_SHA held the tag object, the check would fail closed, never pass by mistake. Whether Actions sets GITHUB_SHA to the commit for annotated tags isn't checkable here; publishing.md:55 uses a lightweight tag. 3. Cheaper alternatives to re-running all of CI: require a successful CI run on GITHUB_SHA (untested), or add just the missing Node 20 test and Inspector gates to the release job. 4. If finding 27 splits release.yml into jobs, put the `needs:` on the first job. The `./.github/workflows/ci.yml` reference only works after step 2 moves the files, as the verifier says.

arbitration.rationale:
The two agents agree on every fact, and I re-checked each one myself. They disagree only on the label. I side with the verifier: confirmed, severity minor. The facts are certain. Where to draw the line between "confirmed" and "needs owner decision" is a judgment call, which is why my confidence is medium.

Why confirmed and not an owner decision:
1. The rule is already written down. publishing.md:52 says "Merge to `main`, then tag the merge commit." The owner-approved plan also wanted the release tooling to check "the packed entry booting on Node 20 and 22" (plan.md:134). The release only ever uses Node 22: release.yml:20 sets it, and pack-mcpb.mjs:75 starts the bundle with whatever Node is running.
2. The step with no guard can't be undone. npm never reuses a name and version, even after an unpublish. The registry rejects a version it already holds.
3. The smallest fix only enforces what publishing.md:52 already says: refuse a tag whose commit isn't on main. It sets no new policy. plan.md records no decision on release gating, and nothing in it conflicts with the fix. What remains for the owner is how far to go: re-run CI, protect main, or add an approval step. The verdict rules let a confirmed finding carry that kind of question.

The auditor's points make a mistake less likely: one collaborator, Claude asks before any tag (plan.md:188), and the local checks in publishing.md:37-51. They lower the severity. They don't close the gap.

What the finding overstates:
- "Any v* tag" is wrong. release.mjs:25-28 stops any tag that isn't v<plugin version>.
- "Without CI's checks" is only partly true. validate.mjs runs (release.mjs:30), including the version-sync check (validate.mjs:182-192) and the stale generated-file check (:215-217). The Node 22 MCP tests run twice, the second time through prepublishOnly (mcp/package.json:48).
- What's actually skipped: the script tests, `claude plugin validate`, Node 20 and the Inspector gates. Only Node 20 and the Inspector gates matter for the npm package. `claude plugin validate` mostly covers the plugin, which ships from main.
- "Goes to npm" only holds once NPM_TOKEN is set (release.yml:49-52), and the repo has no secrets today. A version can still be used up in the registry after a manual npm publish, the first option in publishing.md:20.

The real exposure is small. The workflows are parked, so nothing runs until step 2. Once they run, two plain mistakes get through:
- tagging the head of the version-bump branch. CLAUDE.md:64 says to use Squash and merge, so that commit never lands on main.
- tagging main while its CI is red, for example with Node 20 broken even though engines says >=20.
arbitration.decisive_evidence:
The workflows:
- release.yml:5-7 runs on `tags: ['v*']`. :20 sets `node-version: 22`. :22-29 run npm ci, build and test, then `node scripts/release.mjs --tag "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"`. Nothing checks that the commit is on main or that CI passed. `git log --follow` shows the file unchanged since 7fb1b1a.
- ci.yml has checks that release.yml lacks: the script tests (:25), `claude plugin validate . --strict` (:28-31), `node: [20, 22]` (:39) and `npm run test:inspector` (:51-53).
- The npm package claims Node 20 support: mcp/package.json:35-37 sets engines `>=20`, and mcp/README.md:48 says "needs Node.js 20 or later".

In my copy (a git archive of HEAD):
- `node scripts/release.mjs --tag X` with v9.9.9, v0.1.0-rc.1, v0.1, v0.1.0.1, V0.1.0 and v: each prints "does not match plugin version v0.1.0" and exits 1. No dist/ is written.

Checks of the fix:
- Compare API: main...4ba0a01 gives identical 0 0. main...3956d22 gives ahead 31 0. 3956d22...main gives behind 0 31. cli/cli trunk...(the v2.89.0 commit) gives behind 0 1492. registry main...(the v1.8.6 commit) gives behind 0 20. main...7036772, which isn't pushed, gives 404.

- re-run-workflows-and-jobs.md:20: a re-run uses the same GITHUB_SHA.

findings.fix_assessment: Correct, with two adjustments. First, give the calling `ci` job `permissions: contents: read`, and move the write permissions from the workflow level to the release job. The docs say a calling job without permissions passes the default token permissions; ci.yml's own `contents: read` would downgrade them anyway, so this is belt and braces. Second, `uses: ./.github/workflows/ci.yml` only resolves after step 2 moves the files out of .github/pending-workflows/. The ancestry check is sound: I tested the statuses live, and it fails closed when the API call fails. Putting it in its own job ahead of ci would fail faster, but that's optional. Checks in my copy: the YAML parses and the status logic works under bash -e. Not linted: actionlint isn't installed, and plan.md asks for it.
findings.proposed_fix:
Apply this with step 2 or after it. `./.github/workflows/ci.yml` only resolves once the files are in .github/workflows/.
1. ci.yml: add `workflow_call:` under `on:`.
2. release.yml: set the workflow-level `permissions:` to `contents: read`. Add two jobs before `release`, so a wrong tag fails in seconds:
   on-main:
     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
     steps:
       - name: The tagged commit is on main
         env:
           GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
         run: |
           status="$(gh api "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/compare/main...${GITHUB_SHA}" --jq .status)"
           case "${status}" in
             identical|behind) ;;
             *) echo "::error::${GITHUB_REF_NAME} (${GITHUB_SHA}) is not on main (compare status: ${status})"; exit 1;;
           esac
   ci:
     needs: on-main
     uses: ./.github/workflows/ci.yml
     permissions:
       contents: read
   On the `release` job, add `needs: ci` and job-level `permissions:` with `contents: write` and `id-token: write`.
3. docs/publishing.md:62: say that the workflow first stops unless the tagged commit is on main, then runs the CI checks, and only then publishes. In step 5, add that a tag on an unmerged commit is refused.
4. Run actionlint on both files before pushing (plan.md:135). It isn't installed here, so the fix has only been tested by parsing the YAML and running the on-main step with a stub gh.
If you decline the CI re-run, keep the on-main job and put `needs: on-main` on `release`. If finding 27 splits release.yml into more jobs, put the `needs:` on its first job.
owner_questions: Should every release require the tagged commit to be on main? That rules out a hotfix release from a branch. Should the full CI run again inside the release? That adds several minutes, and a flaky test blocks the release until you re-run it. Optionally, a protected 'release' environment with you as the required reviewer would pause each publish for your approval. Since main is unprotected, 'on main' doesn't mean reviewed: do you also want branch protection on main?

Should the release workflow enforce the release rules in publishing.md? (a) Refuse a tag whose commit isn't on main. This is cheap, but rules out releasing a hotfix from a branch. (b) Re-run the full CI (Node 20, the Inspector gates, plugin validate) before publishing. This adds a few minutes, and a flaky test or a failed claude-code install would block the release until you re-run it. (c) Since main is unprotected, do you also want branch protection, so that 'on main' means reviewed? I recommend (a) now; (b), or just a Node 20 step, is optional.

1. Should every release re-run the full CI on the tagged commit first? It adds a few minutes, and the release then depends on the claude-code npm install. A flaky failure stops the run before anything is published, and "Re-run failed jobs" re-runs only the failed jobs and the jobs after them, on the same commit. The cheaper choice is to trust main's CI and only check that the commit is on main, but that would still publish a tag on a main commit whose CI failed.
2. Will you ever want to release a hotfix from a branch? The on-main check forbids it, as publishing.md:52 already does on paper.
3. Optional: do you want branch protection with required checks on main, so that "on main" also means CI passed? Do you want each publish to wait for your approval in a protected "release" environment?

findings.title: Nothing tells the maintainer to move the parked workflows, and the docs describe them as already running
findings.summary: All four workflows sit in .github/pending-workflows/, where GitHub doesn't run them. GitHub lists 0 workflows and 0 runs for the repository, and its main branch holds only README.md. Yet docs/publishing.md:11-13 and :62, CONTRIBUTING.md:25 and scripts/release.mjs:2-3 describe the workflows as active. One sub-claim no longer holds: handoff step 2 (.claude/CLAUDE.md:55), there since 34d9caa, does say to move them and update the docs. This finding overlaps 34.

claims.claim: The workflows are parked in .github/pending-workflows/, and GitHub doesn't run them there.
claims.evidence: `git ls-files .github` lists the four pending-workflows files, and `git log --all -- .github/workflows` finds no commits. workflow-syntax.md:29: "You must store workflow files in the `.github/workflows` directory of your repository." `gh api .../actions/workflows` -> total_count 0; `.../actions/runs` -> 0.

claims.claim: No file in the repo says they must be moved, and a repo-wide search for 'pending-workflows' finds nothing.
claims.evidence: At HEAD, .claude/CLAUDE.md:55 says "Move `.github/pending-workflows/*.yml` to `.github/workflows/`", and :51 mentions the folder too. The same step was already in 34d9caa (`git show 34d9caa:.claude/CLAUDE.md`, line 53), the commit that stored this review. The claim was true of the tree the reviewer saw: 7fb1b1a has no reference. The maintainer docs still don't say it.

claims.claim: publishing.md says the Release workflow publishes when you push a v* tag, so a maintainer following it would push a tag and nothing would publish.
claims.evidence: docs/publishing.md:11 "The Release workflow, when you push a `v*` tag"; :12-13; :62 "Watch the Release workflow." GitHub has 0 workflows, 0 tags and 0 releases.

claims.claim: CONTRIBUTING.md:25 says 'CI runs the same ones'.
claims.evidence: CONTRIBUTING.md:25: "Run these before opening a pull request. CI runs the same ones."

claims.claim: release.mjs:3 names .github/workflows/release.yml, which doesn't exist.
claims.evidence: scripts/release.mjs:2-3: "Publishing itself ... happens in .github/workflows/release.yml, which calls this first."

claims.claim: npm trusted publishing also needs the file in .github/workflows/.
claims.evidence: npm/documentation trusted-publishers.mdx:50: "The workflow file must exist in `.github/workflows/` in your repository". The project doesn't use trusted publishing yet; publishing.md:22 says release.yml would need changes for it.

findings.reproduction:
Repository and GitHub state:
$ git ls-files .github -> .github/pending-workflows/{ci,evals,release,verify-data}.yml
$ git log --all -- .github/workflows -> (no commits)
$ gh api repos/vipul-goel/prompt-engine/actions/workflows -> total_count 0; actions/runs -> 0; tags -> 0; releases -> 0
$ gh api 'repos/vipul-goel/prompt-engine/contents?ref=main' -> README.md only
$ gh api contents/.github on the remote branch (at 3956d22) -> pending-workflows only

GitHub docs, workflow-syntax.md:29: "You must store workflow files in the `.github/workflows` directory of your repository."

Repository docs and code:
- docs/publishing.md:11 "The Release workflow, when you push a `v*` tag"; :12-13 "The Release workflow"; :62 "Watch the Release workflow."
- CONTRIBUTING.md:25 "CI runs the same ones."
- scripts/release.mjs:2-3 "happens in .github/workflows/release.yml, which calls this first"

History of the handoff note:
$ git grep -n pending-workflows HEAD -> .claude/CLAUDE.md:51 and :55, and .claude/handoff/*.json only
$ git show 34d9caa:.claude/CLAUDE.md -> line 53: "3. Move the parked workflows. Move `.github/pending-workflows/*.yml` to `.github/workflows/`."
$ git grep pending-workflows 7fb1b1a -> nothing

npm docs, npm/documentation content/packages-and-modules/securing-your-code/trusted-publishers.mdx:50: "The workflow file must exist in `.github/workflows/` in your repository"
findings.refutation:
The move is already planned, in handoff step 2 (.claude/CLAUDE.md:55) and in plan.md:92, which places the workflows in .github/workflows/. So the problem is known and scheduled, not overlooked, but the docs stay wrong until the move lands.

The practical harm is small. Nothing has been released, and the owner is asked before any tag (plan.md:188). A tag push that does nothing would be noticed at once. The only collaborator is the owner, and there are 0 forks.

I checked for a fix after 34d9caa: no change to .github, release.mjs or these doc lines.

audit.reasoning:
All four workflows are only in .github/pending-workflows/. GitHub runs workflow files only from .github/workflows (workflow-syntax.md:29), and it lists 0 workflows and 0 runs for this repository. publishing.md:11-13 and :62, CONTRIBUTING.md:25 and release.mjs:2-3 describe the workflows as active, so a tag pushed today would publish nothing.

The headline sub-claim, "no file in the repo says they must be moved", is false at HEAD and was already false at 34d9caa. .claude/CLAUDE.md:55 (step 2) says to move them. That text arrived in 34d9caa itself, as step 3, in the same commit that stored this review. It was renumbered in 3956d22 and expanded in 7036772. The reviewer's tree (7fb1b1a to d63abbf) had no mention, and the maintainer docs still have none.

What remains is the same defect as 34; record them together. The fix is handoff step 2, so no interim doc text is needed.

Minor: nothing has been released, and only the owner has access.
audit.checks_run:
- `git ls-files .github` lists only the four pending files. `git log --all -- .github/workflows` is empty.
- `git grep pending-workflows` finds nothing at 7fb1b1a or d63abbf. At 34d9caa and HEAD it finds only .claude/CLAUDE.md and the handoff JSON files.
- Read every version of .claude/CLAUDE.md: 34d9caa line 53 (step 3), 3956d22 line 52 (step 2), HEAD lines 51 and 55.
- GET requests: 0 workflows, 0 runs, 0 tags, 0 releases, 0 forks. main holds only README.md. On the remote branch (still at 3956d22), .github holds only pending-workflows.
- Docs: workflow-syntax.md:29. npm/documentation trusted-publishers.mdx:50 and :399. In events-that-trigger-workflows.md, pull_request uses the merge commit and doesn't run while the PR has a merge conflict. `git merge-base --is-ancestor 4ba0a01 HEAD` is true, so a PR to main has no conflict.
- In a throwaway git repo, tried the verifier's `git mv` command and a rename of the whole folder.
- In a copy with the folder renamed to .github/workflows: validate.mjs OK, build.mjs --check up to date, and `claude plugin validate . --strict` passed (local check only, no model calls).
audit.evidence_errors: None in the facts. The proposed command fails as written (see below).
audit.fix_corrections:
- `git mv .github/pending-workflows/*.yml .github/workflows/` fails: "fatal: destination '.github/workflows/' is not a directory". Use `git mv .github/pending-workflows .github/workflows`, or run `mkdir -p .github/workflows` first. After the rename, validate, build --check and `claude plugin validate --strict` all still pass in a copy.
- The ordering question needs no owner answer for the docs. They need no interim text as long as step 2 lands before the merge to main.
- ci.yml:3-6 runs only on pull_request and on pushes to main. So step 2's "push, and get CI passing" (CLAUDE.md:55) won't happen on a plain branch push; it needs a pull request.

findings.fix_assessment:
The reviewer proposes a doc item now, to be removed after the move. If step 2 lands before the PR to main, that item would be added and removed on this same branch. The real fix is step 2: it makes publishing.md, CONTRIBUTING.md:25, CHANGELOG.md:34 and release.mjs:2-3 true as written.

Facts that matter for step 2:
- ci.yml:3-6 runs only on push to main and on pull_request, so pushing the branch alone runs no CI.
- GitHub's event table says a pull_request run uses the PR's merge commit, so a PR that adds the files should run CI on itself. Not verified.
- evals.yml and verify-data.yml can be started by hand only once they're on the default branch (manually-run-a-workflow.md:26).
- plan.md:135 asks for an actionlint check, which hasn't run. actionlint isn't installed here, and the reviewer's run was blocked.
findings.proposed_fix:
Do handoff step 2 after the 1c workflow fixes: `git mv .github/pending-workflows/*.yml .github/workflows/`, push, and open the PR so ci.yml runs. Add no interim doc text.

Only if the move has to wait past the merge to main:
- Add a first item to docs/publishing.md "One-time setup": "Move the workflows from `.github/pending-workflows/` to `.github/workflows/`. GitHub runs workflows only from there."
- Change CONTRIBUTING.md:25 to "CI runs the same ones once the workflows are in `.github/workflows/`."
owner_questions: Should step 2 (moving the workflows) come right after 1c and before 1d, so the docs need no interim wording?
ci.yml runs only on pull requests and pushes to main, so CI can't run on a plain push of this branch. May the session open a draft PR to main at step 2, instead of waiting for step 5?

findings.title: CI, release and data-check workflows sit in .github/pending-workflows/, but the docs say they run
findings.summary: Same core as 33: GitHub runs none of the four parked workflows, while CONTRIBUTING.md:25, docs/publishing.md:11-13, :62 and :98, and CHANGELOG.md:34 describe CI, release and the monthly check as running. The first-release gap is also real. CHANGELOG.md:7 reads "## [0.1.0] - not yet released", and publishing.md:36 only covers moving "Unreleased" entries. `node scripts/version.mjs 0.1.0` prints no CHANGELOG reminder, because the heading already exists.

claims.claim: GitHub Actions only runs workflow files from .github/workflows/, and all four are under .github/pending-workflows/.
claims.evidence: Same evidence as 33: workflow-syntax.md:29; `git ls-files .github`; GitHub lists 0 workflows.

claims.claim: So no CI runs on pull requests, a v* tag publishes nothing, and the monthly check never opens an issue.
claims.evidence: `gh api .../actions/workflows` -> total_count 0; `.../actions/runs` -> 0. The repository has 0 tags, 0 releases and 0 issues.

claims.claim: CONTRIBUTING, publishing.md and CHANGELOG describe the workflows as active, and no doc mentions the pending folder.
claims.evidence: The workflows are described as active in CONTRIBUTING.md:25; docs/publishing.md:11-13, :24, :62, :94 and :98; and CHANGELOG.md:34, "CI, release and monthly data re-verification workflows." (the reviewer's :29, moved by later MCP lines). The handoff notes mention the pending folder at .claude/CLAUDE.md:51 and :55, but no user or maintainer doc does.

claims.claim: Nothing prompts the maintainer to put a date on 0.1.0.
claims.evidence: CHANGELOG.md:7; docs/publishing.md:36; scripts/version.mjs:76 checks only `includes("## [0.1.0]")`. In a scratch copy, `node scripts/version.mjs 0.1.0` printed no reminder, while `0.2.0` printed 'Next: add a "## [0.2.0] - YYYY-MM-DD" section'. No other script, test or workflow reads CHANGELOG.

findings.reproduction:
Workflow state: as in 33. The files are only in .github/pending-workflows/, and GitHub lists 0 workflows and 0 runs.

Doc lines:
- CONTRIBUTING.md:25 "CI runs the same ones."
- docs/publishing.md:11-13, :62, :98
- CHANGELOG.md:34 "CI, release and monthly data re-verification workflows."
- CHANGELOG.md:7 "## [0.1.0] - not yet released"
- docs/publishing.md:36 "Move the "Unreleased" entries under a `## [0.2.0] - YYYY-MM-DD` heading."
- scripts/version.mjs:76 `readFileSync(changelog, 'utf8').includes(`## [${next}]`)`

In a scratch copy, set up as a git repo with one commit:
$ node scripts/version.mjs 0.1.0 -> "... skills/prompt-engine/SKILL.md → 0.1.0 / Then run the checks and tag v0.1.0 (see docs/publishing.md)." No CHANGELOG reminder, and no file changed.
$ node scripts/version.mjs 0.2.0 -> "Next: add a "## [0.2.0] - YYYY-MM-DD" section to CHANGELOG.md."
$ git grep -n -i changelog HEAD -- scripts/ .github/ -> scripts/version.mjs:75-77 only

Proposed check, tested in a copy:
- 0.1.0 undated -> reminder
- 0.1.0 dated 2026-11-10 -> none
- 0.2.0 missing -> reminder
- 0.1.10 is not matched by a 0.1.1 heading
$ node scripts/validate.mjs -> OK with and without the change
$ node --test scripts/test/*.test.mjs -> 31/32 with and without the change. The one failure is version.test.mjs "sets the version everywhere and the repository still validates".
findings.refutation:
The move is planned in handoff step 2, so the main claim is known and scheduled, but still true at HEAD.

The reviewer's "major" overstates it. Nothing has been released, only the owner has write access, and step 2 fixes the docs by making them true.

For the first-release part: release.yml:36 builds the release notes with `--generate-notes`, not from CHANGELOG, so an undated heading affects only people reading CHANGELOG.

I checked changes since 34d9caa. CHANGELOG gained MCP lines, which moved :29 to :34; the cited lines are otherwise unchanged.

audit.reasoning:
Same core as 33. GitHub runs none of the parked workflows. Yet CONTRIBUTING.md:25, publishing.md:11-13, :62, :94 and :98, and CHANGELOG.md:34 describe CI, the release and the monthly check as running. Handoff step 2 makes them true, and nothing changed since 34d9caa.

The first-release gap is real but small:
- CHANGELOG.md:7 reads "## [0.1.0] - not yet released".
- publishing.md:36 only covers moving "Unreleased" entries.
- version.mjs:76 only checks that the heading exists.

In a copy, `version.mjs 0.1.0` printed no reminder and changed no file, while `0.2.0` printed one. release.yml:36 builds the notes with `--generate-notes`, so only people reading CHANGELOG see the undated heading.

Minor, not major.
audit.checks_run:
- Read CONTRIBUTING.md:25, publishing.md:11-13, :24, :36, :62, :94 and :98, CHANGELOG.md:7 and :34, version.mjs:75-78 and release.yml:36.
- Checked the same lines at 34d9caa. The CHANGELOG line was :29 then.
- Ran `node scripts/version.mjs 0.1.0` and `0.2.0` in separate copies of HEAD. 0.1.0 printed no CHANGELOG reminder, and diff -rq showed no changed files. 0.2.0 printed the reminder.
- Tested the verifier's dated-heading regex:
  - an undated 0.1.0 heading gives a reminder;
  - a dated one gives none, also with CRLF line endings;
  - a 0.1.10 heading doesn't satisfy 0.1.1.
- Applied the regex in a copy and ran `node --test scripts/test/*.test.mjs`: 31/32, the same single failure in version.test.mjs as without the change. A grep shows no test reads the reminder text.
audit.fix_corrections: The verifier's three items work as tested. For item 1, use `git mv .github/pending-workflows .github/workflows`, because the `*.yml` form fails (see 33).

findings.fix_assessment:
The move is right, and it is handoff step 2, as in 33. The interim wording is only needed if the move waits. The reviewer's publishing.md line for the first release is right.

I'd also make version.mjs look for a dated heading, so it reminds on the first release too. Tested in a copy:
- An undated 0.1.0 heading gives the reminder, and a dated one gives none.
- A missing 0.2.0 gives the reminder.
- A 0.1.1 heading doesn't satisfy 0.1.10.
validate passes, and node --test gives 31/32 with or without the change; the one failure is the known version.test.mjs symlink failure. No test pins the reminder text.

validate.mjs lints only SKILL.md and universal/prompt-engine.md, so these doc and script changes touch no lint, budget or contract check.
findings.proposed_fix:
1. Do handoff step 2: move the workflows to .github/workflows/. That makes CONTRIBUTING.md:25, publishing.md and CHANGELOG.md:34 true.
2. In docs/publishing.md:36, add: "For the first release, replace "not yet released" in the `## [0.1.0]` heading with the date."
3. In scripts/version.mjs:76-77, replace the `includes` test with a regex built from `next` that requires a dated heading on its own line. For 0.1.0 that is /^## \[0\.1\.0\] - \d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/m. When it fails, print: Next: give CHANGELOG.md a "## [x.y.z] - YYYY-MM-DD" heading with the release date.
Tested code: <scratch>/work/verify-workflows-other/sim34b/scripts/version.mjs lines 75-79.

findings.title: README's first paragraph says it works in ChatGPT, Gemini, Cursor and any MCP client, which compatibility.md marks as untested or secondary
findings.summary: README.md:5 still says "It works in Claude, Claude Code, ChatGPT, Gemini, Codex, GitHub Copilot, Cursor and any MCP client." The repo's own status page marks only Claude Code as tested. Claude.ai, Codex, Gemini CLI and Copilot are "✓ docs", ChatGPT and the Gemini app are "? in those apps", and the npm package doesn't exist yet. One sub-claim is out of date: Cursor's own docs now list the skill folders, so by the repo's labels Cursor is "✓ docs", but compatibility.md:25 still says "~ secondary".

claims.claim: README.md:5 states support for all these apps as fact.
claims.evidence: README.md:5 "It works in Claude, Claude Code, ChatGPT, Gemini, Codex, GitHub Copilot, Cursor and any MCP client." `git diff 34d9caa HEAD -- README.md docs/install.md docs/compatibility.md` is empty, so this is not a regression and was never fixed.

claims.claim: ChatGPT and the Gemini app are not checked in those apps.
claims.evidence: docs/compatibility.md:26 "✓ tested (Claude, tools disabled) / ? in those apps … A manual check in ChatGPT and Gemini is pending." The checklist in docs/manual-checks.md:5-61 is still unticked.

claims.claim: Codex and Copilot are checked against docs but not tested.
claims.evidence: docs/compatibility.md:21 and :23 "✓ docs". :5 defines "✓ docs" as "confirmed in the vendor's own documentation or shipped code, not tested here".

claims.claim: Cursor rests on secondary sources only.
claims.evidence: docs/compatibility.md:25 and docs/install.md:93 still say secondary. But cursor.com/docs/context/skills (fetched 2026-11-03) lists `.agents/skills/` (project) and `~/.agents/skills/` (user), and says "For compatibility, Cursor also loads skills from Claude and Codex directories: .claude/skills/, .codex/skills/, ~/.claude/skills/, and ~/.codex/skills/." By the repo's labels, Cursor is now "✓ docs". It is still untested.

claims.claim: The MCP package isn't published.
claims.evidence: `npm view prompt-engine-mcp` returns E404 on 2026-11-03, and the GitHub releases list is empty. No test runs the server in an MCP client app: mcp/test/ uses the SDK client and the Inspector only. So "any MCP client" is a protocol-level expectation, not a tested result.

claims.claim: README.md:87 promises that unverified details are marked as unverified.
claims.evidence: README.md:87 "Those are marked as unverified in the docs instead of being presented as facts." CLAUDE.md's honesty rule says the same.

claims.claim: (Extra, not in the finding) "Claude" in the list is also docs-only.
claims.evidence: docs/compatibility.md:18 lists Claude.ai, Desktop and mobile as "✓ docs". docs/install.md:67 says they "can't be tested from this repository's automation".

findings.refutation: I checked whether the line changed after 34d9caa: it didn't. I looked for any recorded run in ChatGPT or Gemini: none exists, and compatibility.md:26 says the check is pending. plan.md:42-45 says unverified platform facts ship as "check the tool's current docs", never as facts, which supports the finding rather than overriding it. Cursor's docs refute the Cursor sub-claim today, but that doesn't help ChatGPT, Gemini or "any MCP client". The universal prompt is plain text (5,765 characters) and will probably work in other chatbots, so the harm to users is small. The defect is the stated certainty in the most-read sentence.

The sentence breaks README.md:87 ("marked as unverified in the docs instead of being presented as facts") and the hard honesty rule in .claude/CLAUDE.md.

This is not an owner decision. plan.md:42-48 says unverified platform facts ship "never as facts". Claude wrote the line in 7fb1b1a7, and it is unchanged since 34d9caa.

One sub-claim is stale: Cursor's own docs now list its skill folders. The practical harm is small, because the universal prompt is plain text. The defect is the stated certainty.

findings.title: 'Don't install it twice' describes the wrong duplicate, misses the real ones and gives no way out
findings.summary: README.md:48 and docs/install.md:3 say that adding the plugin on Claude.ai and in Claude Code gives two copies. Claude Code's docs and the 2.1.317 binary say otherwise: the local copy loads, and the Claude.ai copy is listed as not loaded. The docs do enable real overlaps they never mention. A skill zip uploaded on Claude.ai also syncs into Claude Code and loads next to the plugin. Copilot in VS Code and Cursor read Claude's skill folders as well as `~/.agents/skills/`. And `npx skills add` installs into Claude Code without asking when it's the only agent found, or with `-y`. No doc says how to remove a copy. Confidence is medium because all of this comes from vendor docs and code; I couldn't run a claude.ai sync here.

claims.claim: The README's example (Claude.ai plugin plus Claude Code plugin gives two copies) is wrong.
claims.evidence: code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/loading.md, "Name conflicts", item 5: "When an enabled plugin from any other origin matches its name, Claude Code loads that plugin and reports the synced copy as not loaded. To use the claude.ai copy instead, disable your own copy." The Claude Code 2.1.317 binary contains `Synced plugin "…" shadowed by local copy …`, which marks the synced copy "dropped". The rule compares manifest names, and both copies are named "prompt-engine" (.claude-plugin/plugin.json; the marketplace entry is also "prompt-engine").

claims.claim: The Claude.ai copy is then silently unused.
claims.evidence: It is reported, not silent. The 2.1.317 binary shows a /plugin row: `"…" from claude.ai not loaded — "…" on this machine has the same name and takes precedence`. It also gives a hint: "To use the claude.ai copy instead, run `claude plugin enable …`, then disable or remove …".

claims.evidence: claude.com/docs/skills/overview.md says "A plugin's skills appear on Your skills too, labeled with the plugin's name", but no doc covers a same-name upload. docs/manual-checks.md:72 expects two copies, but that check hasn't been run, and testing it needs a Claude.ai account.

claims.evidence: code.claude.com/docs/en/skills.md, "Skills synced from claude.ai": synced skills "include the ones you create or turn on in your claude.ai settings". The same page's "Resolve skills that share a name" table says: "A plugin skill and a skill at any of the locations above | Both load, because plugin skills are namespaced". This applies when Claude Code signs in with the same claude.ai account. Untested here.

Synced plugins need a claude.ai sign-in and Claude Code 2.1.273 or later, and the docs don't say when the name-conflict rule arrived, so an older client might load both copies. That isn't checkable here, and 2.1.317 drops the synced copy. The advice "don't install twice" is still sound, so the harm is a wrong reason plus missing guidance, not bad advice. plan.md:136 asks for a "don't install twice" note; the fix keeps such a note, so there's no conflict. The finding's word "silently" is wrong. Nothing here changed since 34d9caa.

audit.reasoning:
The note's example is imprecise, and the overlaps where both copies really load are missing.

**The example.** Claude Code's docs (plugins/loading.md, "Name conflicts", item 5) say a same-named local plugin loads and the synced claude.ai copy is reported as not loaded. The code agrees. In the 2.1.317 binary, the synced copy is marked "dropped" with the message `Synced plugin "…" shadowed by local copy`. I also read the 2.1.273 binary from npm. 2.1.273 is the first version that syncs, per the docs, and it has the same rule. So no syncing version loads both copies. README.md:48 is literally true that two copies get installed and listed, but it implies two working copies.

**The missed overlaps:**
- A skill zip uploaded on claude.ai also syncs into Claude Code and loads next to the plugin. skills.md's last same-name row says the synced skill "is then listed and runs only under its full name".
- `npx skills add` writes `.claude/skills/prompt-engine` next to the plugin. The skills.md row for a plugin skill and a local skill says "Both load". skills 1.7.6 installs into Claude Code without asking when `~/.claude` is the only agent it finds, or with -y.
- Cursor and VS Code's local sessions read both `~/.claude/skills` and `~/.agents/skills`.
- The plugin and the .mcpb bundle both run in Claude Desktop chat. README.md:42 and :45 offer both.

**No way out.** No doc says how to remove a copy; manual-checks.md:72 only says "remove one".

This is not an owner decision: plan.md:136 asks for a "don't install twice" note, and the fix keeps one. Severity is minor, because the advice itself is still right. Medium confidence: everything comes from vendor docs and code; no app was run.
audit.checks_run: Fetched code.claude.com's plugins/loading.md, skills.md and plugins/install.md; claude.com's skills/overview, plugins/overview, plugins/platform-support and connectors/custom/add-unlisted; VS Code's agent-skills page; GitHub's Copilot skills pages; and Cursor's skills page. The help text in 2.1.317 lists `plugin enable <plugin>`, `plugin disable [plugin]` and `plugin uninstall <plugin>`. Ran npm pack skills@latest (1.7.6) and read dist/cli.mjs: claude-code detection (:1590-1598), runAdd (:5207-5236), selectAgentsInteractive (:4958), promptForAgents (:4925) and the canonical-folder logic (:2291-2298). Read .claude-plugin/*.json: both names are "prompt-engine". Applied corrected text in scratch: checks unchanged, all links and anchors resolve.

1. The refutation says an older client "might load both copies" and that this "isn't checkable here". It was checkable: the 2.1.273 binary has the same drop rule.
2. Claim 1 ("holds") overstates. Two copies are installed and listed in /plugin; only one loads.
3. For the zip-sync overlap, the cited row ("A plugin skill and a skill at any of the locations above | Both load") doesn't cover synced skills. The right row is the last one ("…the short name of a skill synced from your claude.ai account"). The conclusion is the same.

audit.fix_corrections:
1. "Install it once per app" invites the exact double install the note warns about, since Claude.ai and Claude Code are two apps. Keep plan.md:136's "Don't install it twice". At install.md:3, write "Pick one option… Some options reach more than one app, so a second install can give you two copies."
2. Add when sync applies: Claude Code 2.1.273 or later, signed in with the claude.ai account (not an API key).
3. Optional, not checkable here: when Claude Code is a target, `npx skills add` makes `.claude/skills/prompt-engine` a symlink to the canonical `.agents/skills/prompt-engine` (cli.mjs:2291-2298, 2420-2440). Cursor and VS Code read both folders; whether they show the skill twice is untested.
The rest of the verifier's section, including the `-a codex` advice and the status line, matches the code and docs. I tested the corrected text in scratch; checks unchanged.

First, "deselect Claude Code when `npx skills add` offers it" fails in the common cases: skills 1.7.6 offers no choice when Claude Code is the only detected agent, or with -y. Naming agents with `-a <agent>` is what works. Second, it misses that the skill zip also syncs into Claude Code next to the plugin. Third, it pastes the same long paragraph into both README.md and install.md. Append this section to docs/install.md:

"## Install it once" — Some options reach more than one app, so a second install can give you two copies:
- **Claude.ai plugin and Claude Code plugin.** A plugin you add on Claude.ai also loads in Claude Code as `prompt-engine@synced` when you sign in there with that Claude.ai account. If you also installed `prompt-engine@vipul-goel`, Claude Code runs your local copy and lists the Claude.ai copy as not loaded. To use the Claude.ai copy instead, run `claude plugin uninstall prompt-engine@vipul-goel`.
- **Skill zip.** A skill you upload on Claude.ai also loads in Claude Code when you sign in there with that account, next to the plugin's skill rather than in place of it. Use the plugin or the zip, not both.

- **Copied folders.** GitHub Copilot in VS Code and Cursor also read Claude Code's skill folders, `~/.claude/skills/` and `.claude/skills/`. If you copied the skill there, don't copy it into `~/.agents/skills/` as well.

End the section with a status line: "checked on 2026-11-03 against Claude Code's plugin and skills docs, claude.com's plugin docs, VS Code's and Cursor's skills docs, and skills 1.7.6; not tested here."

findings.title: Docs tell users to run `npx -y prompt-engine-mcp`, a package name nobody has published yet
findings.summary: The docs tell users to run `npx -y prompt-engine-mcp`: README.md:45, docs/install.md:103 and seven lines in mcp/README.md. That name is still unpublished on npm (E404 on 2026-11-03), and the repository is public. Whoever publishes it first controls what the documented command runs, and could also block the owner's own npm and MCP Registry publish. The exposure today is small: `main` holds only a stub README, GitHub code search indexes only the default branch, and the repo has 0 stars and 0 forks. It becomes real when this branch merges to `main`.

claims.claim: The npm name is still free.
claims.evidence: `npm view prompt-engine-mcp` returns E404, and `curl https://registry.npmjs.org/prompt-engine-mcp` returns 404. Variants that differ only in punctuation (promptenginemcp, prompt_engine_mcp, prompt.engine.mcp, promptengine-mcp, prompt-enginemcp) all return 404, so npm's similar-name rule won't block the owner. `prompt-engine` exists, but it's an unrelated 2022 library.

claims.claim: The repository is public.
claims.evidence: `gh api repos/vipul-goel/prompt-engine` returns "visibility":"public".

claims.claim: The docs tell users to run `npx -y prompt-engine-mcp`.
claims.evidence: README.md:45, docs/install.md:103, docs/publishing.md:71, and mcp/README.md:23, :33, :43, :48, :120 and :142. The finding named only the first two, plus publishing.md:19.

claims.claim: `-y` skips npx's install prompt.
claims.evidence: npm 11.19.0's npm-exec.md:28 says the prompt "can be suppressed by providing either `--yes` or `--no`". But :29 adds: "When standard input is not a TTY or a CI environment is detected, `--yes` is assumed." MCP clients start stdio servers over pipes, so dropping `-y` wouldn't protect them. It matters only for terminal runs such as `npx -y prompt-engine-mcp --http`.

claims.claim: The "after the first release" caveat is easy to miss.
claims.evidence: In README.md the caveat sits at :48, after the table. docs/install.md:103 puts it in the same sentence, and mcp/README.md:16 puts it at the top of Install. Either way, a caveat doesn't stop someone else claiming the name.

claims.claim: A squatter would control the command and could block the owner's release.
claims.evidence: mcp/server.json "packages" registers npm identifier "prompt-engine-mcp" 0.1.0, and plan.md:38 says the registry needs mcpName to match. If someone else owns the name, the owner can't publish there, and the registry entry fails.

claims.claim: How exposed it is today.
claims.evidence: `main` is "Initial commit" 4ba0a01, and its README is just "# prompt-engine". GitHub's code search docs say "Only the *default branch* is indexed for code search." The repo has stars 0, forks 0, watchers 0.

findings.refutation: The caveats at README.md:48, install.md:103 and mcp/README.md:16 tell users the package isn't out yet. They don't stop a squatter, though, and after a squat the command would simply work, running someone else's code. Today's exposure is limited, because the docs aren't on `main` and code search can't find them, which lowers the urgency but doesn't remove the defect. The lines are unchanged since 34d9caa (mcp/README.md had the same commands then, at :23, :113 and :127).

audit.reasoning:
**The name is still free.** npm returns E404, the registry returns 404, and the punctuation variants also return 404. The docs give `npx -y prompt-engine-mcp` at:
- README.md:45
- docs/install.md:103
- docs/publishing.md:71
- mcp/README.md:23, :33, :43, :48, :120 and :142
All of these were present at 34d9caa.

**`-y` doesn't matter for MCP clients.** npm's libnpmexec skips the install prompt when stdin isn't a TTY (index.js:298, no-tty.js).

**The exposure exists today, not only after merge.** The pushed branch (tip 3956d22) is public. Its docs/publishing.md:19 says the name "was unclaimed", and its .claude/handoff/repo-review-partial.json calls it "a package name nobody has published yet". Discoverability is low: 0 stars, 0 forks, and code search covers only the default branch.

**The release workflow would not catch a squat.** The parked release.yml:45-47 treats any existing version as already published ("already on npm", exit 0), without checking who published it.

The fix needs the owner's npm account (.claude/CLAUDE.md step 5), so this is confirmed with an owner question.
audit.checks_run: Ran `npm view prompt-engine-mcp` and curl against registry.npmjs.org for the name and five variants (all 404; `prompt-engine` is an unrelated 2021 package). `gh api` GET calls on the repo: visibility public, stars 0. Branches: main is "Initial commit" 4ba0a01, and the branch tip is 3956d22. Fetched publishing.md and the review file from the public branch. Ran git grep at HEAD and at 34d9caa. Read .github/pending-workflows/release.yml, mcp/server.json and mcp/package.json. Read npm 11.19.0's npm-exec.md:28-29 and libnpmexec/lib/index.js:288-310. Fetched GitHub's about-github-code-search page. Ran `npm view prompt-engine@0.0.31 _npmUser` to confirm the publisher field exists.
audit.evidence_errors:
1. "It becomes real when this branch merges to main" understates the risk. The public branch already names the package and says it is unclaimed.
2. The code-search quote isn't on the page as quoted. The page says "We currently only support searching for code on the default branch of a repository." The meaning is the same.
audit.fix_corrections:
1. npm never lets a version be reused. Publishing 0.1.0 early from the branch would freeze 0.1.0 at that code, and release.yml:45-47 would then skip publishing the tagged code. Either publish 0.1.0 from the exact commit that will be tagged, with no later mcp/ changes, or claim the name now with a lower version such as 0.0.1.
2. Add a publisher check at release.yml:45-47. For example, `npm view "prompt-engine-mcp@${version}" _npmUser` must name the owner's npm account, or the step fails; then the registry step (:59-69) doesn't run either. Inference, not tested: if a squatter copied the public mcpName, the registry's mcpName check (:57) could pass and point the owner's entry at their code.
3. In publishing.md, drop "before the docs reach main". Say to claim the name now, because the public branch already names it.
4. The fallback at mcp/README.md:33, :43 and :48 is JSON or the Windows `cmd /c` form. Those lines need `"command": "node", "args": ["/path/to/prompt-engine/mcp/dist/cli.js"]` plus a build step first, not a text substitution.

findings.fix_assessment: The reviewer's main remedy is right and closes the risk: claim the name before merge by publishing 0.1.0 by hand, as docs/publishing.md:20 describes. That fits publishing.md:20 ("Do this before you push the tag") and the release workflow's skip-if-published step. It needs the owner, because npm isn't logged in on this Mac and CLAUDE.md step 5 says to ask before publishing. The reviewer's fallback undercounts: replacing the command means eight edits across three files, not two. Dropping `-y` alone would not help. I tested the publishing.md wording in a scratch copy, and the checks didn't change.
findings.proposed_fix:
1. The owner publishes `prompt-engine-mcp` 0.1.0 before the PR to `main` merges. From a clean checkout: `npm login`, then `cd mcp && npm ci && npm publish --access public`. Then confirm with `npm view prompt-engine-mcp`.
2. docs/publishing.md:19: after "was unclaimed when this was written." add: "Claim it before the docs that tell users to run `npx -y prompt-engine-mcp` reach `main`: until then, anyone can publish a package under that name."
3. CLAUDE.md step 5: add a pre-merge check that `npm view prompt-engine-mcp` shows the owner's package.
4. Only if the owner merges first: replace `npx -y prompt-engine-mcp` with `node /path/to/prompt-engine/mcp/dist/cli.js` at README.md:45, docs/install.md:103 and mcp/README.md:23, :33, :43, :48, :120 and :142 until the package exists.
owner_questions: Will you publish `prompt-engine-mcp` to npm yourself before the PR to `main` merges? That needs `npm login` on your Mac, or an NPM_TOKEN secret. Or should the docs switch to the from-clone command until the first release?

Will you claim `prompt-engine-mcp` on npm now (it needs `npm login` on your Mac)? If yes, should it be 0.1.0 from the final PR head right before merge, or a placeholder such as 0.0.1 now? Or should the docs use the from-clone command until the first release?

findings.title: The privacy note implies the MCP server never sees your prompt, but check_prompt and ask_user do, and hosting isn't covered
findings.summary: README.md:101 is literally true: `enhance_prompt` takes only mode and target. But `check_prompt` receives the draft enhanced prompt, and `ask_user` receives the questions and, when a form is shown, the user's answers and notes. Run locally, all of that stays on the machine. On a server someone else hosts, it passes through that server, and neither README says so; mcp/README.md:172 also leaves out `ask_user`. The claims about logging and outbound calls hold.

claims.claim: `enhance_prompt` doesn't receive the prompt.
claims.evidence: mcp/src/server.ts:120-123 has EnhanceInput = { mode?, target? }, and :345 is `async ({ mode, target }) => text(buildBrief(...))`.

claims.claim: `check_prompt` receives the full draft.
claims.evidence: mcp/src/server.ts:179: `prompt: z.string()…describe('The draft enhanced prompt (the full prompt, not the whole reply).')`, used by the handler at :402-403. mcp/src/brief.ts:115 tells the model to "Optionally call check_prompt on your draft full prompt". This was the same at 34d9caa (server.ts:148 there).

claims.claim: `ask_user` carries the questions and the user's answers.
claims.evidence: There's a nuance: answers reach the server only in form mode. mcp/src/server.ts:371-373 reads `inputResponse(ctx.mcpReq.inputResponses, FORM_KEY)` and then `mapFormAnswers(questions, response.content)`, and notes can be up to 1,000 characters (questions.ts:12). In text mode the server only returns questionsText, and the user's reply goes to the model.

claims.claim: The README offers a hosted HTTP mode.
claims.evidence: The root README mentions HTTP only in its test list (README.md:85). It links the MCP guide (README.md:45), whose "Self-hosting over HTTP" section is mcp/README.md:117-166. docs/publishing.md:15 and :85-87 list an optional hosted server. There's no public hosted instance today.

claims.claim: mcp/README.md states this more precisely.
claims.evidence: mcp/README.md:172 "Only `check_prompt` sees a draft, and only when the model calls it." It is more precise, but it also leaves out `ask_user`.

claims.claim: The logging claim holds.
claims.evidence: mcp/src/log.ts:1-3 and describeError at :15-44 keep request text out of log lines. The CLI logs only through describeError (cli.ts:104, :141). worker.ts:37-38 logs only the ALLOWED_HOSTS warnings. mcp/wrangler.jsonc:8 has "observability": { "enabled": false }.

claims.claim: (Extra) It makes no outbound network calls.
claims.evidence: Grepping mcp/src for fetch(, http(s).request, net.connect and the like finds only `mcp.fetch(request)` at cli.ts:149 and worker.ts:56. That's the SDK handler for inbound requests, not an outbound call.

findings.refutation: The sentence is literally true, which is why I rate this minor. What misleads is the "doesn't even" implication, and it matters exactly in the hosted case, where `check_prompt` and form-mode `ask_user` send user content to the host. I checked whether HEAD changed these inputs since 34d9caa: it didn't. brief.ts:116 tells the model "doesn't receive the user's prompt unless you pass a draft to check_prompt"; that's model-facing and accurate in the narrow sense, so it needs no change.

audit.reasoning:
README.md:101 says "Its main tool doesn't even receive your prompt text." That is literally true: `enhance_prompt` takes only mode and target (mcp/src/server.ts:120-123, handler at :345). But the other tools do receive user content:
- `check_prompt` takes the full draft (server.ts:179, handler at :402), and mcp/src/brief.ts:115 invites the model to call it.
- `ask_user` receives the questions. In form mode, the user's answers and notes (up to 1,000 characters, mcp/src/questions.ts:12) come back to the server (server.ts:371-373).

Run locally, this is harmless. On a hosted copy (mcp/README.md:117-166; docs/publishing.md:15 and :85-87), those inputs reach the host, and neither README says so. mcp/README.md:172 also leaves out ask_user.

The logging and no-outbound-call claims hold. mcp/src/log.ts:15-44 keeps request text out of log lines. Every CLI log line either goes through describeError (cli.ts:104, :141, :181) or is the usage message (:74). worker.ts:37-38 logs only the ALLOWED_HOSTS warnings, and wrangler.jsonc:8 turns observability off. The SDK's own console calls are registration warnings. There are no outbound calls in mcp/src.

Unchanged since 34d9caa (old server.ts:148 and mcp/README.md:146). Not an owner decision: plan.md:98 already treats privacy in hosted mode as a goal.
audit.checks_run: Read server.ts, brief.ts, questions.ts, log.ts, cli.ts, worker.ts, wrangler.jsonc and manifest.json. Grepped mcp/src for fetch, http(s).request, net.connect, WebSocket and child_process; the only fetch is inbound `mcp.fetch(request)`. Grepped @modelcontextprotocol/server 2.4.0's dist for console calls. Ran `git show 34d9caa` on server.ts and mcp/README.md. Applied the corrected text in scratch: checks unchanged, links resolve. manifests.test.ts only checks server.json's description length.
audit.evidence_errors:
Minor:
- cli.ts also logs at :181 (listen failure, through describeError) and :74 (usage). Neither carries request text.
- "There's no public hosted instance today" can't be checked here. All I can say is that the repo documents none.
audit.fix_corrections:
1. "Run locally, all of this stays on your machine" overclaims. The draft and the form answers are also part of the conversation your AI app sends to its model provider: the answers go back to the model as the tool result. Use instead: "A server on your own machine sends none of this anywhere; if you connect to a copy someone else hosts, those calls go to their server."
2. Say "your answers and notes", not just "your answers".
3. Optional: mcp/README.md:5 and mcp/manifest.json:7 also say "makes no network calls", but with --http the server takes network requests. Align them with "never calls a model or any other service". No test pins either string.

findings.fix_assessment: The reviewer's text matches the code, with one imprecision: "ask_user carries … your answers" is true only when a form is shown. It also leaves mcp/README.md:172, which has the same gap for `ask_user`, unchanged. README.md isn't validated or linted, so there's no budget risk. I applied my version in a scratch copy, and the checks didn't change.
findings.proposed_fix:
README.md:101: "The skill and the universal prompt are just instructions: your prompts go only to the AI app you already use. The MCP server never calls a model or any other service, needs no API key and doesn't log prompts. Its main tool, `enhance_prompt`, never receives your prompt. `check_prompt` receives a draft when the model calls it, and `ask_user` receives the questions and, when your app shows them as a form, your answers. Run locally, all of this stays on your machine; if you connect to a copy someone else hosts, those calls go to their server."

mcp/README.md:172: append "`ask_user` receives the questions and, when your app shows a form, returns your answers and notes. On a server someone else hosts, those calls pass through their server."

findings.title: Test-status claims don't match the recorded evidence: missing trigger set, in-sample score, wrong re-run row, install source
findings.summary: Confirmed on this branch. No commit contains the 24-request trigger set that CHANGELOG.md:31 and README.md:82 present. By compatibility.md's own numbers, its held-out sentence (:56) gives no evidence for the shipped description. The Claude Code row (:15) was tested from the feature branch, and the documented unpinned command fails today. The re-run row's cost and without-skill figures (:40) can't be re-checked on this Mac.

claims.claim: (a) CHANGELOG and README present a 24-request trigger set that isn't in the repository.
claims.evidence: CHANGELOG.md:31 'trigger tests for the skill description (24 requests…)' sits under '### Added' (:11). README.md:82 says '24 requests, half of them near-misses'. git ls-files finds only 3 trigger eval cases. Across every commit, 'should_trigger' appears only in .claude/handoff/repo-review-partial.json. compatibility.md:51,53 name at most 6 requests plus the 'prompt-engine:' class. .claude/CLAUDE.md:62 tells sessions to re-run the trigger tests from 'the eval set … described in docs/compatibility.md'. That can't be done.

claims.claim: (b) compatibility.md:56 is garbled and suggests the shipped description was validated on held-out requests.
claims.evidence: The sentence says the first description 'never saw' 8 requests 'during tuning', but the first description was never tuned. By :53 (21/24) and :56 (all 8 held-out passed), its 3 misses were among the 16 tuning requests, so the whole 21-to-24 gain is in-sample. skill-creator run_loop.py on this Mac holds out int(12*0.4)=4 per class (:37-38, :254) and picks best by test score only (:218). Python's max keeps the first tie (my check printed 1). So an original at 8/8 would itself be the loop's best_description. The shipped description (55a5b2b, unchanged since) differs from the original.

claims.claim: (b) The shipped description was hand-written (candB.json) after all 24 results were seen, and the loop's final description differs from it.
claims.evidence: None of the tuning files (desc-tune, eval-set.json, candB.json) are on this Mac. The claim is consistent with the selection-rule point above.

claims.claim: (c) The re-run row should read 6 cases, 6/6, without-skill 1/3 (mean 0.67), $0.68.
claims.evidence: evals/results/ doesn't exist on this Mac. The 998e0c8 message says 'the 5 affected cases now pass', which supports the row's 5. If the total was $0.685, the row's $0.69 is normal rounding and the reviewer's $0.68 is not. In 2.1.317, `claude plugin eval --help` says --ablation defaults to 'with-without', so the row's '—' means the run used --ablation none or the data was dropped. No record shows which.

claims.claim: (d) The interactive test installed from the feature branch, and the documented command can't work yet.
claims.evidence: main has one commit, 4ba0a01 'Initial commit', holding README.md only, so no install could have come from main. I ran `claude plugin marketplace add vipul-goel/prompt-engine` with a throwaway CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR. It printed '✘ Failed to add marketplace: Marketplace file not found at …/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json' and exited 1. The `#claude/gallant-thompson-eblqe0` form succeeded. .claude/CLAUDE.md:63 also re-runs the smoke test 'from the branch'.

findings.refutation: (a) I searched every commit, the ignored files and this Mac for the set and found none. Partial refutation: three trigger cases are in the repo (README.md:81 already mentions them), but they aren't the 24-request set. (b) I read the sentence charitably, as being about the loop's first iteration. By the doc's own numbers, the held-out set still can't tell the two descriptions apart. I also checked that the description hasn't changed since 55a5b2b. (c) The commit message backs the count of 5. Nothing on this Mac confirms or refutes the cost or the missing without-skill arm. (d) I checked whether main ever held the plugin: it has one README-only commit. The unpinned command fails. Nothing has been fixed since 34d9caa.

audit.reasoning:
Confirmed. Parts (a) and (b) hold on HEAD. Part (c) can't be checked on this Mac. Part (d) has the right facts, but the row's wording isn't false.

(a) Holds. CHANGELOG.md:31 lists "trigger tests for the skill description (24 requests…)" under "### Added" (:11), next to things that are in the repo (17 eval cases, the two-turn test). No commit has the set: across all 33 commits, `should_trigger` appears only in .claude/handoff/repo-review-partial.json. git ls-files finds only the 3 trigger eval cases. evals/results/ doesn't exist, and no ignored file holds the set. compatibility.md:51 and :53 name 6 requests plus the "prompt-engine:" class, so the instruction at .claude/CLAUDE.md:62 can't be followed.
- Partial refutation: plan.md:139 says to run run_loop "from a scratch directory" and never asks for the set to be committed. So the missing set fits the plan. The defects are the "Added" wording and CLAUDE.md:62.
- README.md:82 reports a real one-off result (the reviewer's checked_ok saw 24/24). It only needs a "one-off" note.

(b) Holds. :56 gives the 8/8 to "the first description", which was never tuned, so the sentence says nothing about the shipped description. The current description also passed 24/24, so on either reading the held-out set can't tell the two apart. The verifier read the run_loop.py on this Mac correctly:
- :37-38 hold out int(12*0.4)=4 per class.
- :218 picks the best iteration by test score alone.
- Python's max keeps the first of a tie (my check printed 1).
So in the stock loop, an original scoring 8/8 would be best_description. The shipped description (55a5b2b, unchanged since) differs from the original. compatibility.md:52 says the loop was "adapted", so this fits the reviewer's "picked by hand" claim but doesn't prove it.

(c) Can't be checked here. The row's 5 matches the 998e0c8 message ("the 5 affected cases now pass") and the 5 cases that commit touched: 3 histories, the secret-redaction grader, and research through SKILL.md. But the SKILL.md:64 change also affects question-round cases such as coding-vague, so a sixth re-run is plausible. Nothing here settles the cost or the missing without-skill results.

(d) The facts hold:
- main's only commit is 4ba0a01, holding README.md. The contents API returns 404 for .claude-plugin/marketplace.json on main. The only other branch is the feature branch, so any GitHub install came from it.
- I re-ran both commands. Unpinned: "✘ Failed to add marketplace: Marketplace file not found…", exit 1. With #claude/gallant-thompson-eblqe0: "✔ Successfully added marketplace".
- But :15 says only "installed from this repository's marketplace on GitHub", which is true of the branch. What it leaves out: README.md:41's unpinned commands were never run, and 998e0c8 changed SKILL.md:64, :93 and :99 after the test (see finding 43).

Not already fixed: `git diff 34d9caa HEAD` is empty for compatibility.md and README.md. The CHANGELOG line only moved from :26 to :31.

Severity: "major" is arguable. These are accuracy problems in the test-status docs, which matter under the honesty rule, but no result was invented.

findings.title: The prior-art claim isn't what the cited release notes say, and time-sensitive pages have no checked-on date
findings.summary: README.md:91 credits Anthropic's release notes with retiring the 'Console prompt improver and generator'. The cited page never says 'improver'. It retires the legacy Workbench and the experimental generate, improve and templatize prompt APIs. The next sentence about other 'enhance prompt' buttons has no source, and install.md has no checked-on date. README.md:42 and install.md:59 give only the old toggle name; Anthropic now says it is called 'Create and edit files' in the updated Settings layout.

claims.claim: The cited release notes never mention a prompt improver.
claims.evidence: Release notes downloaded today as .md and HTML: 0 matches for 'improver'. The only related entries are relnotes.md:247-248 under '### July 17, 2026' and relnotes.md:197 under '### August 18, 2026' ('Workbench is now playground').

claims.claim: The notes announce the retirement of the legacy Workbench and of the experimental prompt-tools API endpoints.
claims.evidence: July 17, 2026: 'The legacy Workbench ... is being sunset with access ending on August 17, 2026' and 'The experimental prompt tools APIs for generating, improving, and templatizing prompts (/v1/experimental/generate_prompt, /v1/experimental/improve_prompt, and /v1/experimental/templatize_prompt) are being retired along with the Workbench on August 17, 2026.'

claims.claim: Implied by README.md:91: the Console UI's prompt improver and generator were retired.
claims.evidence: Checking needs a Console login. Indirect signs only: Anthropic's old docs pages .../prompt-engineering/prompt-improver and /prompt-generator now redirect to 'Prompting best practices'. Help Center 8606378 (modified 2026-10-19) says 'Workbench is now retired' but names neither tool. A web search found no Anthropic statement naming them. plan.md:40 records only 'Console prompt generate/improve endpoints'.

claims.claim: 'Most remaining enhance-prompt buttons ... rewrite silently' has no source.
claims.evidence: README.md:91 has no link. git grep finds no source in docs/sources.md or .claude/handoff/. Whether the claim is true wasn't checked: it generalises over many products.

claims.claim: The prior-art descriptions have no as-of date.
claims.evidence: README.md:89-97 has no date. Side check: all four descriptions still match their READMEs today. prompt-master README:86 says 'max 3 questions' and :91 'one clean copyable block'. claude-code-prompt-improver README:15 says 'asks 1-6 grounded questions only when the prompt is genuinely vague'. prompt-architect README:3 says '31 frameworks' and :101 has 'Quality Scoring System'. mattpocock/skills grilling SKILL.md:8 works in 'rounds' and :15 gives 'your recommended answer'.

claims.claim: docs/install.md has no checked-on date, unlike compatibility.md, sources.md and publishing.md.
claims.evidence: grep -E '20[0-9]{2}|checked|last updated|as of' docs/install.md finds nothing. compatibility.md:3 has 'Last updated: 2026-10-29'; sources.md:3 and publishing.md:3 have 'checked on 2026-10-29'. install.md:55 has a version only: 'tested here with Claude Code 2.1.312'.

claims.claim: The toggle is now called 'Create and edit files' in the updated Settings layout, and README and install.md give only the old name.
claims.evidence: Help Center 12512180 and 12111783 (both modified 2026-10-30): 'Code execution and file creation (called Create and edit files in the updated Settings layout)'. README.md:42 and install.md:59 use only the old name, as do compatibility.md:18 and plan.md:35.

claims.claim: Extra, not in the finding: install.md:59's owner and plan wording is out of date.
claims.evidence: install.md:59 says 'on Team and Enterprise plans an Owner enables it'. Help Center 12111783 says the feature 'is enabled by default for Team plan organizations' and 'for new Enterprise plan organizations', and owners can disable it. The skills article now says 'Skills are available for users on Free, Pro, Max, Ultra, Team, and Enterprise plans'; install.md:59's plan sentence doesn't mention Ultra. I didn't check whether other Anthropic pages still disagree on plans.

findings.refutation: I asked whether the README is a fair paraphrase. The retired APIs were the API side of the Console's generate and improve tools, and the old docs pages now redirect, so the Console features are probably gone. But no Anthropic page I found says so, and the README attributes the claim to release notes that don't make it. sources.md:31 and plan.md:40 already word it accurately, so only the README drifted. The files are unchanged since 34d9caa, so nothing was fixed. The old toggle name is still on Anthropic's pages (and on mobile), so the docs are incomplete for the new layout rather than wrong. The toggle is on by default for most accounts, which lowers the impact. Severity stays minor.

audit.reasoning:
README.md, docs/install.md, docs/sources.md and docs/compatibility.md are unchanged since 34d9caa (`git diff --stat 34d9caa HEAD` on them is empty), so nothing was fixed.

Core defect holds. README.md:91 says the 'Console prompt improver and generator were retired in August 2026, according to Anthropic's release notes'. I fetched the notes today (overview.md, 136,891 bytes, and the HTML): 0 matches for 'improver'. The only related entries are July 17, 2026 (overview.md:247-248: the legacy Workbench is sunset and the experimental generate/improve/templatize prompt APIs are retired on Aug 17) and Aug 18 (overview.md:197: 'Workbench is now playground'). So the README credits the notes with a claim they don't make.

I tried to refute it by finding any Anthropic statement that the Console UI tools were retired. I found none:
- Help Center 8606378 (modified 2026-10-19) says 'Workbench is now retired' and never mentions generating or improving prompts.

findings.refutation: "Tested automatically" could mean "checked by a script rather than by eye". But under "Testing status" in a user-facing README it reads as ongoing automated testing, while the run is manual, billed and stale. The owner's honesty rule calls for precise wording. compatibility.md's "✓ tested" label ("exercised by this repository's automation or by hand during development") does fit, so compatibility.md:26 needs only the date and the tools caveat, not a new label. The wrong count (47) is the reviewer's error, not the docs'.

findings.title: The Agent SDK advice leaves out Read, which the skill needs to load its references
findings.summary: install.md:72 tells Agent SDK users who pass their own tools list to include Skill and AskUserQuestion, but not Read. In the SDK, tools sets the whole list of available built-in tools, and Anthropic's SDK doc says skills run with the session's tools. A list without Read therefore leaves the skill unable to read the reference files that SKILL.md:43-47 says to read in its first turn. The effect on output wasn't measured; that needs billed runs.

Claude Code skills doc: allowed-tools 'grants permission for the listed tools'; it doesn't add tools. Not run end to end, because an SDK session makes billed calls.

The score caveat, rubric anchors, question protocol and domain checklists live only in references (for example output-format.md:68), so some drift is likely.

findings.refutation: I looked for anything that would put Read back. The SDK's skills option only adds Skill entries to allowedTools and never touches the tools list. The skill's allowed-tools: Read frontmatter only grants permission, per the Claude Code doc. The CLI help says --tools sets the available built-in tools. I couldn't run an SDK session, because it makes billed calls, so the end-to-end effect is untested. The drift claim is overstated, since SKILL.md carries the contract headings itself. install.md is unchanged since 34d9caa.

audit.reasoning:
install.md:72 (unchanged since 34d9caa) says: 'If you pass your own `tools` list, include `Skill`, plus `AskUserQuestion` if your app handles questions.' It doesn't mention Read. Yet SKILL.md:43-47 makes the skill Read output-format.md, blueprint.md, questions.md and a domain pack in its first turn, and install.md:52 tells headless users to allow Skill and Read.

What the SDK does with these options:
- In SDK 0.3.312 and 0.3.317 sdk.d.ts, `tools` (:1692 and :1716) is the 'base set of available built-in tools'.
- `allowedTools` (:1635 and :1659) says 'To restrict which tools are available, use the `tools` option instead', and that passing 'Skill' there is deprecated.
- `skills` (:2353 and :2377) is 'the single place to turn skills on'.
- These three blocks are identical in both versions.
- In both versions, core.mjs passes a tools array as `--tools a,b`. `skills` becomes `Skill(name)` entries in allowedTools and is also sent in the initialize request. Neither touches `tools`.

I looked for anything that would bring Read back and found nothing. In CLI 2.1.317 (read statically from the binary), the --tools parser returns toolsToDisallow: every built-in tool not in the list. Those tools are then stored as alwaysDenyRules.toolsNarrowing. The SDK permissions doc says denying a whole tool removes its definition from the request, and that deny rules are checked before allow rules. A skill's `allowed-tools` only adds permission. The Claude Code skills doc says it 'grants permission for the listed tools', and the SDK skills doc says 'Skills run with the session's tools'. So `allowed-tools: Read` can't restore Read. sdk.d.ts does say 'List Grep/Glob here or in allowedTools to get them', but the CLI code limits that rule to Grep and Glob; it doesn't cover Read.

Limits:
- I didn't run an SDK session, because those calls are billed.
- The drift claim is unmeasured. SKILL.md carries the contract strings itself (validate passes), so the headings would survive; the rubric, score caveat and checklists live only in references/.

Severity: minor, because many custom tool lists already include Read.

In sdk.d.ts, read the tools, allowedTools and skills blocks and diffed each between versions: identical. Searched core.mjs and sdk.mjs for the skills→allowedTools mapping, the --tools push and the initialize-request skills field. Fetched both CHANGELOGs with gh api: TypeScript 0.2.120 adds `skills` and 0.2.133 deprecates 'Skill' in allowedTools; Python 0.1.62 adds `skills`. curl code.claude.com agent-sdk/skills.md (lines 32, 46, 348 and 350), skills.md (lines 404 and 617) and agent-sdk/permissions.md (the deny→allow→canUseTool order; whole-tool deny removes the definition). Read the CLI 2.1.317 binary with a Python mmap search: the --tools help text, the parser's return {toolsToDisallow: ...}, and alwaysDenyRules:{...toolsNarrowing:x}.
audit.evidence_errors:
1. 'skills only extends allowedTools' is incomplete. core.mjs also sends the list in the initialize request (`skills:Array.isArray(this.initConfig?.skills)?this.initConfig.skills:void 0`), and that is how unlisted skills are hidden. It still never adds tools, so the conclusion stands.

2. The quote 'When omitted, discovered skills are enabled' comes from agent-sdk/skills.md:32, not sdk.d.ts. sdk.d.ts says 'omitted (default): no SDK auto-configuration ... this is **not** "skills off."' The two agree.

Everything else checks out: the line numbers, the CHANGELOG entries, skills.md:46 and :350, the Claude Code skills.md:617, and the CLI help.
audit.fix_corrections:
1. 'SDK 0.2.120 or later' is the TypeScript version. The Python SDK added `skills` in 0.1.62 (its CHANGELOG). Write '(TypeScript SDK 0.2.120 or later, Python SDK 0.1.62 or later)', or drop the version.

2. Replace 'without a permission prompt' with 'pre-approve the skill call'. SDK apps have no built-in prompt: per the permissions doc, calls nothing else resolves go to canUseTool, and in dontAsk mode they are denied.

3. Optional: Save to file (SKILL.md:99) is offered only where the skill can write files. Mention Write only if SDK apps should get that option.

These are docs only, so no check is affected.

findings.fix_assessment: The reviewer's first sentence is right. The second, 'Recent SDK versions can also turn it on with skills: ['prompt-engine']', is imprecise in three ways. Skills are already on by default ('When omitted, discovered skills are enabled'). What the option actually does is pre-approve the Skill call, by adding Skill(prompt-engine) to allowedTools, and hide every other skill. And per Anthropic's SDK doc, it doesn't replace listing Skill in an explicit tools list. Name the version, 0.2.120 or later, instead of 'recent'. Tested in a copy: checks unchanged.

claims.claim: inspector-gates.mjs exits 1 below 22.19.
claims.evidence: mcp/scripts/inspector-gates.mjs:17 'if (major < 22 || (major === 22 && minor < 19))', and :19 calls process.exit(1). Reproduced with faked versions: 20.20.2 and 22.18.0 printed 'needs Node >= 22.19' and exited 1. 22.19.0 and 24.21.0 passed the check.

claims.claim: Inspector 2.13.0 declares engines >=22.19.0.
claims.evidence: mcp/package-lock.json says '>=22.19.0', and so does undici 8.12.3. `npm view @modelcontextprotocol/inspector@2.13.0 engines` gives '>=22.19.0', and 2.13.0 is still the latest.

claims.claim: mcp/README.md and ci.yml state the requirement.
claims.evidence: mcp/README.md:177 'Node.js 22.19 or later for the full tool chain'. ci.yml:51-52 'needs Node >= 22.19' with 'if: matrix.node == 22'.

claims.claim: The root scripts pass on Node 20.
claims.evidence: Node 20 isn't installed on this Mac. A static scan of scripts/ found no Node 22+ APIs.

claims.claim: (added) Node 20 is end-of-life.
claims.evidence: nodejs/Release schedule.json lists v20 'end':'2026-04-30'. The runtime dependencies need only >=20 (lockfile), which matches mcp/package.json engines '>=20'.

findings.refutation: Neither CONTRIBUTING nor publishing.md mentions 22.19 or points to mcp/README.md's requirement. The gate's error names the needed version, so the failure is quick to understand, which lowers the severity but doesn't remove the contradiction. The text is unchanged since 34d9caa. CI isn't affected: it pins Node 22 for the inspector and release steps.

audit.reasoning:
Confirmed, minor. CONTRIBUTING.md:18 says "Node.js 20 or later (22 recommended)". CONTRIBUTING.md:35-38 tell anyone who changed mcp/ to run `npm test && npm run test:inspector`. docs/publishing.md:44 runs the same command and gives no Node version anywhere.

The gate at mcp/scripts/inspector-gates.mjs:17-19 exits 1 below 22.19. In my copy I faked process.versions.node with a preload:
- 20.20.2, 22.0.0 and 22.18.0 print "The MCP Inspector CLI needs Node >= 22.19" and exit 1.
- 22.19.0 and 24.21.0 pass the version check, then fail to resolve the Inspector (the copy has no node_modules).

Version facts:
- `npm view` shows Inspector 2.13.0 is the latest, with engines >=22.19.0.
- In the lockfile, the Inspector and undici 8.12.3 declare >=22.19.0.
- `npm test` alone also declares a higher floor than 20: vitest 3.2.7 uses vite 7.3.7, which declares "^20.19.0 || >=22.12.0" (declared only; I couldn't run it).
- mcp/README.md:177 and ci.yml:51-52 state the real requirement.
- nodejs/Release schedule.json puts Node 20's end of life at 2026-04-30.

Refutation attempt: :18's second sentence is about scripts/, and the MCP setup bullet (:20) gives no version. So a careful reader might look in mcp/README.md. But CONTRIBUTING doesn't point there, and "22 recommended" suggests any 22 works, which 22.0-22.18 don't. The gate's message makes the failure quick to understand, which is why this is minor.

Not fixed: the same lines were there at 34d9caa.

audit.fix_corrections:
The fix keeps "Node.js 20 or later for the scripts in scripts/". CI doesn't check that: the skill job runs Node 22 only (ci.yml:19). The reviewer's Node 20.20.2 run was at their tree, and lint-rules.test.mjs, validate.test.mjs and version.test.mjs have changed since. My static scan found no APIs newer than Node 20, so the claim is plausible but unverified. When the workflows move (step 2), add Node 20 to the skill job; until then, say the claim is untested on the current tree.
Also add the 22.19 note to .claude/CLAUDE.md:27-30. That checks block runs test:inspector but names Node 22 only, and only for test:worker.

findings.fix_assessment: The reviewer's fix is correct and safe, with two refinements. Drop '22 recommended', because 22.0 to 22.18 fail too. Keep the 'nothing to install at the repository root' sentence. Not checked: npm test may also need Node 20.19 or later on the 20 line, because vite 7.3.7 (pulled in by vitest) declares '^20.19.0 || >=22.12.0'. No check reads these lines. In my copy, build --check, validate and plugin validate --strict pass, and tests stay at 31/32, as in a pristine copy.
findings.proposed_fix: CONTRIBUTING.md:18 → two bullets: '- **Node.js 20 or later** for the scripts in `scripts/`. They use only Node built-ins, so there's nothing to install at the repository root.' and '- **Node.js 22.19 or later** for the MCP server's checks. `npm run test:inspector` runs the MCP Inspector, which needs it, and stops with an error on older versions.' docs/publishing.md, after the mcp code block at :43-45: '   The MCP checks need Node.js 22.19 or later, because `npm run test:inspector` uses the MCP Inspector.'
